from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import datetime
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from sqlalchemy import Boolean, DateTime, String, Text, func
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import UUID as PGUUID
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, relationship

from .base import Base

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .contact import Contact
    from .refresh_token import RefreshToken


class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"

    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True), primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4
    )
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(100), nullable=False)
    phone: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(20), unique=True, nullable=False)
    avatar_url: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text)
    fcm_token: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text)
    fcm_token_updated_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True)
    )
    password_hash: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text)
    is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, nullable=False, default=True)
    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False, server_default=func.now()
    )
    last_seen: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False, server_default=func.now()
    )

    contacts: Mapped[list[Contact]] = relationship(
        "Contact",
        foreign_keys="Contact.user_id",
        back_populates="user",
        lazy="raise",
    )
    refresh_tokens: Mapped[list[RefreshToken]] = relationship(
        "RefreshToken", back_populates="user", lazy="raise"
    )

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"<User id={self.id}>"

1. `http.createServer(cb)` - cb is added as request listener #1
2. `new Server(httpServer, opts)` - engine.io saves [cb], removes cb, adds its own listener


3. Engine.io's listener fires for ALL requests
4. For requests matching `/signal/...`, engine.io handles them (returns 400 for health check)
5. For requests NOT matching `/signal/...`, engine.io calls the original cb

This explains everything! My health check at `/signal/health` is intercepted by engine.io and engine.io returns 400 because `/signal/health` doesn't look like a valid socket.io handshake. Registering the health check handler after socket.io is set up won't work because engine.io only forwards requests that don't match its patterns, not newly added listeners.

I could handle the health check inside engine.io's scope by modifying its check function, but that requires changing engine.io source code. Alternatively, I could move the health check to a different URL like `/health` instead of `/signal/health` and update the Dockerfile and docker-compose accordingly. Another option is to use a different Socket.IO path like `/signal/ws` so the health check URL doesn't match the socket pattern. Or I could try adding a listener before socket.io using `server.on('request', cb)`, though engine.io removes all listeners when it initializes.

Looking at how engine.io actually works, it saves existing listeners before clearing them, then adds its own handler that checks the path and either processes it or calls the saved listeners for non-matching requests. This means I could add my health check handler before socket.io attaches, and engine.io would preserve it in that saved listeners array. I see the core issue now—both engine.io and my new listener will fire for the same request, causing a double-response error. Rather than trying to work around engine.io's listener chain, the cleanest solution is to move the health check endpoint outside the `/signal/...` path entirely to `/health`, and let Nginx handle routing `/signal/health` requests to that endpoint.

Now I'm thinking through how the proxy configuration actually works—the Nginx config can strip the `/signal` prefix when forwarding to the signaling container, so the container only needs to listen on `/health` internally, not `/signal/health`. Nginx will handle the external routing, so the health check endpoint can stay at `/health` internally. The acceptance criterion asking for `GET /signal/health → 200` will work once Nginx proxies `/signal/` to the container and routes `/signal/health` to the internal `/health` endpoint. I briefly considered running the health check on a separate port to avoid any conflicts, but that would require exposing an additional port in docker-compose which adds unnecessary complexity. The simpler approach is to just use `/health` as the endpoint, keeping everything on port 8001.

Now I'm updating the Dockerfile and docker-compose configuration to point their health checks at `/health`, and I'll note in the testing documentation that Nginx will eventually expose this endpoint as `/signal/health` for external access.

**`src/db.js`** — pg Pool with `getUserBrief`, `getFcmToken`, `getContactUserIds`, `insertCallRecord` (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING for idempotent hangup handling).

**`src/callHandler.js`** — Full call lifecycle: `call:initiate` (creates session, relays inline or FCM-queues for offline callee, starts 30s ring timer), `call:answer` (clears timer, updates session to `in-call`, 4h TTL), `call:ice/ice_restart` (trickle relay), `call:reject/hangup` (writes `call_records`, deletes session), `call:busy`.

**`src/presenceHandler.js`** — `presence:update` broadcasts to all contacts with live sessions; `presence:get` returns current presence from Redis.

**`src/typingHandler.js`** — `typing:start/stop` with 5s TTL keys, sorted-pair namespace.

**`src/messageHandler.js`** — `psubscribe` on `msg_delivery:*`, `receipt:*`, `presence:*` → fans out to user rooms as `message:new`, `message:deleted`, `message:ack`, `presence:update`.

**`src/server.js`** — Socket.IO with `path: '/signal'`, WebSocket-only, auth middleware, connection lifecycle (session + presence on connect/disconnect), health at `/health` (not `/signal/health` — engine.io intercepts all `/signal/*` URLs; Nginx will map external `/signal/health` → internal `/health`).

**`Dockerfile`** — Added `COPY config/`, `HEALTHCHECK` using `/health`.

**`docker-compose.yml`** — `signaling` service now depends on `postgres: healthy` (for DB queries), added healthcheck.

1	# Prompt 09 — Coturn TURN/STUN Server Setup
2	
3	Provide the Coturn (TURN/STUN) server setup for FamilyLink. Coturn runs **on the host**
4	(not in Docker) so it can bind the large UDP relay port range cleanly. Produce
5	configuration files and idempotent setup scripts under `coturn/`. Depends on prompt 01.
6	
7	## Goal
8	
9	A working, secured Coturn install whose time-limited HMAC credentials are exactly
10	compatible with FastAPI's `turn_service` (prompt 04): WebRTC clients can use STUN for
11	NAT discovery and TURN as a relay fallback.
12	
13	## Tasks
14	
15	### 1. `coturn/install.sh`
16	
17	An idempotent Bash script (safe to re-run) that:
18	- `apt-get update && apt-get install -y coturn`.
19	- Enables Coturn in `/etc/default/coturn` (`TURNSERVER_ENABLED=1`).
20	- Copies `coturn/turnserver.conf` (templated — see below) to `/etc/turnserver.conf`,
21	  substituting `${VPS_PUBLIC_IP}`, `${DOMAIN}`, `${TURN_SECRET}` from environment
22	  variables or arguments. Refuse to run if `TURN_SECRET` is unset.
23	- `systemctl enable coturn && systemctl restart coturn`.
24	- Prints the verification steps at the end.
25	
26	### 2. `coturn/turnserver.conf` (template)
27	
28	Produce the config with these settings (use placeholders the script substitutes):
29	
30	```ini
31	# Network
32	listening-port=3478
33	tls-listening-port=5349
34	listening-ip=0.0.0.0
35	external-ip=${VPS_PUBLIC_IP}
36	
37	# Realm / identity
38	realm=${DOMAIN}
39	server-name=${DOMAIN}
40	
41	# Auth — time-limited HMAC credentials (REST API style, RFC 5389/8489)
42	use-auth-secret
43	static-auth-secret=${TURN_SECRET}
44	
45	# TLS — shared with Nginx / Let's Encrypt (see prompt 10)
46	cert=/etc/letsencrypt/live/${DOMAIN}/fullchain.pem
47	pkey=/etc/letsencrypt/live/${DOMAIN}/privkey.pem
48	
49	# Relay port range for media (must be open in the firewall)
50	min-port=49152
51	max-port=65535
52	
53	# Security hardening
54	no-multicast-peers
55	no-loopback-peers
56	no-cli
57	denied-peer-ip=10.0.0.0-10.255.255.255
58	denied-peer-ip=192.168.0.0-192.168.255.255
59	denied-peer-ip=172.16.0.0-172.31.255.255
60	no-tlsv1
61	no-tlsv1_1
62	
63	# Quotas / capacity
64	total-quota=100
65	max-bps=1000000          # 1 Mbps per allocation
66	
67	# Logging
68	log-file=/var/log/coturn/turnserver.log
69	simple-log
70	```
71	
72	Notes to embed as comments:
73	- `use-auth-secret` + `static-auth-secret` is the mechanism FastAPI's
74	  `generate_turn_credentials` targets — the username is `{expiry}:{userId}` and the
75	  credential is `base64(HMAC-SHA1(secret, username))`. Do **not** also enable
76	  `lt-cred-mech` with static users; the two mechanisms conflict.
77	- `external-ip` must be the droplet's public IP; on DigitalOcean with a single NIC the
78	  plain form is fine.
79	
80	### 3. `coturn/firewall.sh`
81	
82	A script that applies the required inbound rules (use `ufw`, and also print the
83	equivalent DigitalOcean Cloud Firewall rules as comments since DO firewalls are managed
84	in the dashboard/API):
85	
86	```
87	ALLOW  UDP 3478              (STUN / TURN)
88	ALLOW  TCP 3478              (TURN over TCP — firewall traversal)
89	ALLOW  TCP 5349              (TURNS / TLS)
90	ALLOW  UDP 49152-65535       (TURN media relay)
91	```
92	
93	Keep SSH (TCP 22) and HTTP/HTTPS (80/443) rules intact — the script must not lock the
94	operator out. Print a warning and require a confirmation flag (`--yes`) before applying.
95	
96	### 4. `coturn/verify.md`
97	
98	A short verification guide:
99	- `sudo systemctl status coturn` should be active.
100	- `turnutils_uclient` smoke test against the server.
101	- The browser tool at `https://icetest.info/` or
102	  `https://webrtc.github.io/samples/src/content/peerconnection/trickle-ice/` — enter
103	  the `turn:` URL plus a username/credential pair generated by
104	  `GET /api/auth/turn-credentials`, and confirm a `relay` candidate appears.
105	- `tail -f /var/log/coturn/turnserver.log` during a test call.
106	
107	### 5. Certificate dependency note
108	
109	Coturn's `cert`/`pkey` point at Let's Encrypt files created in prompt 10. Document that
110	`install.sh` should run **after** the certificate exists, or that Coturn will start
111	without TLS (port 5349 down) until certs are issued — and that Certbot's renewal hook
112	(prompt 10) must `systemctl reload coturn` so it picks up renewed certs.
113	
114	### 6. systemd renewal hook
115	
116	Provide `coturn/certbot-deploy-hook.sh` to be placed at
117	`/etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/` that runs `systemctl reload coturn` after a
118	renewal. (Prompt 10 also references this.)
119	
120	## Constraints
121	
122	- Coturn runs on the **host**, not in Docker — do not add it to `docker-compose.yml`.
123	- The auth mechanism must be `use-auth-secret` only; the HMAC algorithm is **SHA-1**
124	  and the secret must equal `TURN_SECRET` from `.env`.
125	- The relay port range and `3478`/`5349` must be open; private peer ranges denied.
126	- Scripts must be idempotent and must never drop the SSH rule.
127	
128	## Acceptance checks
129	
130	1. `coturn/install.sh` (with env set) installs and starts Coturn; `systemctl status
131	   coturn` is active.
132	2. From another machine, a STUN binding request to `stun:DOMAIN:3478` succeeds.
133	3. Credentials from `GET /api/auth/turn-credentials` produce a working `relay` ICE
134	   candidate in the Trickle-ICE web tool.
135	4. `coturn/firewall.sh --yes` opens 3478/5349/49152-65535 and SSH still works.
136	5. Replacing the cert and running the deploy hook reloads Coturn with no downtime.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# coturn/install.sh — Idempotent Coturn install and configuration
#
# Usage:
#   export VPS_PUBLIC_IP=1.2.3.4
#   export DOMAIN=family.example.com
#   export TURN_SECRET=your-secret-here
#   sudo -E bash coturn/install.sh
#
# Or pass variables as arguments:
#   sudo bash coturn/install.sh 1.2.3.4 family.example.com your-secret
#
# Safe to re-run — each step is checked before executing.
# Run AFTER certbot has issued the certificate (see verify.md); Coturn starts
# without TLS (port 5349 down) if the cert files do not exist yet.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

# ── Argument / env handling ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
VPS_PUBLIC_IP="${1:-${VPS_PUBLIC_IP:-}}"
DOMAIN="${2:-${DOMAIN:-}}"
TURN_SECRET="${3:-${TURN_SECRET:-}}"

if [[ -z "$TURN_SECRET" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: TURN_SECRET is required." >&2
  echo "  export TURN_SECRET=<secret>  OR  pass as third argument." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ -z "$VPS_PUBLIC_IP" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: VPS_PUBLIC_IP is required." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ -z "$DOMAIN" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: DOMAIN is required." >&2
  exit 1
fi

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
CONF_TEMPLATE="$SCRIPT_DIR/turnserver.conf"
COTURN_CONF="/etc/turnserver.conf"
COTURN_DEFAULT="/etc/default/coturn"
LOG_DIR="/var/log/coturn"

echo "==> Installing Coturn..."
if dpkg -s coturn &>/dev/null; then
  echo "    coturn already installed, skipping apt."
else
  apt-get update -qq
  apt-get install -y coturn
fi

echo "==> Enabling Coturn service in $COTURN_DEFAULT..."
if grep -qE '^TURNSERVER_ENABLED=1' "$COTURN_DEFAULT" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "    Already enabled."
else
  # Replace or append the directive
  if grep -qE '^#?TURNSERVER_ENABLED' "$COTURN_DEFAULT" 2>/dev/null; then
    sed -i 's/^#*TURNSERVER_ENABLED.*/TURNSERVER_ENABLED=1/' "$COTURN_DEFAULT"
  else
    echo "TURNSERVER_ENABLED=1" >> "$COTURN_DEFAULT"
  fi
fi

echo "==> Creating log directory $LOG_DIR..."
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
chown -R turnserver:turnserver "$LOG_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Writing $COTURN_CONF from template..."
if [[ ! -f "$CONF_TEMPLATE" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: Template not found at $CONF_TEMPLATE" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Substitute placeholders using sed (avoids envsubst dependency)
sed \
  -e "s|\${VPS_PUBLIC_IP}|$VPS_PUBLIC_IP|g" \
  -e "s|\${DOMAIN}|$DOMAIN|g" \
  -e "s|\${TURN_SECRET}|$TURN_SECRET|g" \
  "$CONF_TEMPLATE" > "$COTURN_CONF"

chmod 640 "$COTURN_CONF"
chown root:turnserver "$COTURN_CONF" 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Verifying substitution (no placeholders should remain)..."
if grep -qE '\$\{(VPS_PUBLIC_IP|DOMAIN|TURN_SECRET)\}' "$COTURN_CONF"; then
  echo "ERROR: Unresolved placeholders in $COTURN_CONF" >&2
  grep -E '\$\{' "$COTURN_CONF" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "==> Enabling and restarting Coturn..."
systemctl enable coturn
systemctl restart coturn

echo ""
echo "================================================================"
echo " Coturn installed successfully."
echo "================================================================"
echo ""
echo "Verification steps:"
echo "  1. Check service status:"
echo "       sudo systemctl status coturn"
echo ""
echo "  2. STUN smoke test (install: apt install coturn):"
echo "       turnutils_uclient -T $VPS_PUBLIC_IP"
echo ""
echo "  3. TLS check (requires cert — see verify.md):"
echo "       openssl s_client -connect $DOMAIN:5349 -servername $DOMAIN"
echo ""
echo "  4. Full relay test:"
echo "       See coturn/verify.md for the Trickle-ICE web tool instructions."
echo ""
echo "  5. Watch logs:"
echo "       tail -f $LOG_DIR/turnserver.log"
echo ""
echo "NOTE: If /etc/letsencrypt/live/$DOMAIN/ does not exist yet,"
echo "      port 5349 (TLS) will be down until certs are issued (prompt 10)."
echo "      After cert renewal, run:"
echo "       sudo systemctl reload coturn"
echo "      or install coturn/certbot-deploy-hook.sh to do it automatically."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# coturn/firewall.sh — Open required ports for Coturn with ufw
#
# Usage:
#   sudo bash coturn/firewall.sh --yes
#
# Without --yes the script prints what it would do and exits (dry-run).
#
# Required ports:
#   UDP 3478          STUN / TURN (plain)
#   TCP 3478          TURN over TCP (firewall traversal)
#   TCP 5349          TURNS / TLS
#   UDP 49152-65535   TURN media relay
#
# Ports this script NEVER touches (preserved):
#   TCP 22   SSH
#   TCP 80   HTTP (Nginx / certbot)
#   TCP 443  HTTPS (Nginx)
#
# DigitalOcean Cloud Firewall equivalent rules (manage in the DO dashboard
# or via doctl / Terraform — these are NOT applied by this script):
#
#   Inbound rules:
#     Protocol  Port(s)         Sources
#     UDP       3478            All IPv4, All IPv6
#     TCP       3478            All IPv4, All IPv6
#     TCP       5349            All IPv4, All IPv6
#     UDP       49152-65535     All IPv4, All IPv6
#     TCP       22              (restrict to your IPs in production)
#     TCP       80              All IPv4, All IPv6
#     TCP       443             All IPv4, All IPv6
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

APPLY=false

for arg in "$@"; do
  if [[ "$arg" == "--yes" ]]; then
    APPLY=true
  fi
done

# ── Dry-run notice ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ "$APPLY" != true ]]; then
  echo "DRY RUN — no changes will be made."
  echo "Re-run with --yes to apply."
  echo ""
  echo "Would execute the following ufw commands:"
  echo "  ufw allow 22/tcp        # SSH (ensure not dropped)"
  echo "  ufw allow 80/tcp        # HTTP"
  echo "  ufw allow 443/tcp       # HTTPS"
  echo "  ufw allow 3478/udp      # STUN / TURN"
  echo "  ufw allow 3478/tcp      # TURN over TCP"
  echo "  ufw allow 5349/tcp      # TURNS / TLS"
  echo "  ufw allow 49152:65535/udp  # TURN media relay"
  echo ""
  echo "WARNING: Applying firewall rules can lock you out if SSH is not open."
  echo "Verify 'ufw status' before enabling if ufw is not yet active."
  exit 0
fi

# ── Safety check ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "==> Ensuring SSH (TCP 22) is allowed before any changes..."
ufw allow 22/tcp comment "SSH"

echo "==> Ensuring HTTP/HTTPS are allowed..."
ufw allow 80/tcp  comment "HTTP"
ufw allow 443/tcp comment "HTTPS"

echo "==> Opening Coturn ports..."
ufw allow 3478/udp comment "STUN/TURN"
ufw allow 3478/tcp comment "TURN-TCP"
ufw allow 5349/tcp comment "TURNS-TLS"
ufw allow 49152:65535/udp comment "TURN-relay"

echo "==> Enabling ufw (if not already active)..."
# 'ufw --force enable' is idempotent and won't drop existing connections
ufw --force enable

echo ""
echo "==> Current ufw status:"
ufw status verbose

echo ""
echo "================================================================"
echo " Firewall rules applied successfully."
echo " SSH (TCP 22) is open — you are not locked out."
echo "================================================================"
echo ""
echo "REMINDER: If you use DigitalOcean Cloud Firewall, also add the"
echo "equivalent inbound rules in the DO dashboard (see comments at the"
echo "top of this script). ufw and DO Cloud Firewall operate independently."

# Coturn Verification Guide

## Prerequisites

- `install.sh` has been run and `systemctl status coturn` shows **active (running)**.
- Firewall rules from `firewall.sh --yes` have been applied (ports 3478, 5349, 49152-65535 open).
- DNS for `$DOMAIN` resolves to `$VPS_PUBLIC_IP`.
- TLS certificate exists at `/etc/letsencrypt/live/$DOMAIN/` (prompt 10). Port 5349
  will be down until the cert is issued; all other checks work without it.

---

## 1. Service status

```bash
sudo systemctl status coturn
```

Expected: `active (running)`. If not:
```bash
sudo journalctl -u coturn -n 50 --no-pager
sudo cat /var/log/coturn/turnserver.log
```

---

## 2. STUN smoke test with turnutils_uclient

`turnutils_uclient` is included in the `coturn` package.

```bash
# Plain STUN binding (no auth needed)
turnutils_stunclient $DOMAIN

# TURN allocation with HMAC credentials
# USERNAME format expected by Coturn: "{unix_expiry}:{any_string}"
EXPIRY=$(( $(date +%s) + 3600 ))
USERNAME="${EXPIRY}:smoketest"
# Compute HMAC-SHA1 of username with your TURN_SECRET
CREDENTIAL=$(echo -n "$USERNAME" | openssl dgst -sha1 -hmac "$TURN_SECRET" -binary | base64)

turnutils_uclient \
  -T \
  -u "$USERNAME" \
  -w "$CREDENTIAL" \
  $DOMAIN
```

Expected: allocation succeeds, data relayed, no authentication errors.

---

## 3. TLS / TURNS check (port 5349)

```bash
openssl s_client -connect $DOMAIN:5349 -servername $DOMAIN < /dev/null 2>&1 \
  | grep -E 'Verify|subject|issuer|DONE'
```

Expected: certificate from Let's Encrypt, `Verify return code: 0 (ok)`.

---

## 4. End-to-end relay test with the Trickle-ICE tool

1. Open [https://webrtc.github.io/samples/src/content/peerconnection/trickle-ice/](https://webrtc.github.io/samples/src/content/peerconnection/trickle-ice/)

2. Obtain credentials from the FastAPI server:
   ```bash
   # Register/login first, then:
   curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://$DOMAIN/api/auth/turn-credentials
   ```
   Returns:
   ```json
   {
     "username": "1234567890:userId",
     "credential": "base64string==",
     "ttl": 86400,
     "uris": [
       "stun:family.example.com:3478",
       "turn:family.example.com:3478",
       "turns:family.example.com:5349"
     ]
   }
   ```

3. In the Trickle-ICE tool:
   - Add ICE server: `turn:$DOMAIN:3478`
   - Username: the `username` from the API response
   - Credential: the `credential` from the API response
   - Click **Gather candidates**

4. Expected output: at least one candidate with type **`relay`** appears.
   If only `host` and `srflx` appear, TURN relay is blocked — check the firewall.

---

## 5. Log monitoring during a test call

```bash
tail -f /var/log/coturn/turnserver.log
```

During a call you should see allocation requests, permission grants, and data
channel activity. No `ERROR` or `auth failed` lines should appear.

---

## 6. Certificate renewal verification

After a cert renewal (manual or automatic):

```bash
# Simulate renewal
sudo certbot renew --dry-run

# Or trigger the deploy hook directly
sudo /etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/reload-coturn.sh

# Confirm Coturn reloaded without restarting
sudo systemctl status coturn
# Should still show the original start time, not a new one
```

---

## Certificate dependency note

`install.sh` should be run **after** `certbot certonly` has issued the certificate.
If you install Coturn before the cert exists:
- Coturn starts successfully on port 3478 (STUN/TURN over UDP/TCP).
- Port 5349 (TURNS/TLS) will **not** open until the cert files exist.
- Once the cert is issued, `sudo systemctl restart coturn` will bring 5349 up.
- Going forward, the `certbot-deploy-hook.sh` keeps the cert fresh automatically.

---

## Common issues

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Authentication failed` | `TURN_SECRET` mismatch between Coturn and FastAPI | Verify both use same `TURN_SECRET` from `.env` |
| No `relay` candidate | UDP 49152-65535 blocked | Re-run `firewall.sh --yes`, check DO Cloud Firewall |
| Port 5349 refused | Cert not yet issued | Run `certbot certonly` first (prompt 10) |
| Coturn won't start | Config syntax error | `sudo turnserver -c /etc/turnserver.conf --check` |
| `lt-cred-mech` conflict | Old config leftover | Remove `lt-cred-mech` from `/etc/turnserver.conf` |

# Prompt 10 — Nginx Reverse Proxy & SSL

Implement the production Nginx configuration: TLS termination, reverse proxy to FastAPI
and the Socket.IO signaling server, signed media serving via `auth_request`, security
headers, and Let's Encrypt certificate issuance + auto-renewal. Work in `nginx/` and
`deploy/`. Depends on prompts 01, 06, 08.

## Goal

A single HTTPS domain (`family.example.com`) that routes `/api/` to FastAPI, `/signal/`
to the WebSocket signaling server, and `/media/` to the local media files behind a
signature check — with valid, auto-renewing TLS.

## Tasks

### 1. `nginx/conf.d/familyapp.conf` (replace the prompt-01 placeholder)

Implement:

**Upstreams** with keepalive:
```
upstream fastapi   { server fastapi:8000;   keepalive 32; }
upstream signaling { server signaling:8001; keepalive 32; }
```

**HTTP → HTTPS server (port 80)**:
- `server_name family.example.com;`
- Serve `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` from a webroot path (for Certbot webroot mode).
- Everything else `return 301 https://$host$request_uri;`.

**HTTPS server (port 443, http2)**:
- `ssl_certificate` / `ssl_certificate_key` → Let's Encrypt live paths for the domain.
- `ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;`, modern cipher suite, `ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:50m`,
  `ssl_session_tickets off`, `ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off`.
- Security headers (`always`): `Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000"`,
  `X-Frame-Options DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options nosniff`,
  `Referrer-Policy no-referrer`.
- `client_max_body_size 160M;` (largest upload = 150MB video + overhead).

**`location /api/`** → `proxy_pass http://fastapi;`
- Forward `Host`, `X-Real-IP`, `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`.
- `proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection "";`
- `proxy_read_timeout 300s; proxy_send_timeout 300s;` (large uploads).

**`location /signal/`** → `proxy_pass http://signaling;`
- WebSocket upgrade headers: `proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;`
  `proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";` `proxy_http_version 1.1;`
- Long timeouts: `proxy_read_timeout 3600s;` so idle sockets aren't cut.
- Forward `Host`, `X-Real-IP`.

**`location /media/`** — signed static media:
```
location /media/ {
    auth_request /_media_auth;
    alias /var/app-media/;
    expires 7d;
    add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";
    add_header Accept-Ranges bytes;
}
```
**`location = /_media_auth`** — internal:
```
location = /_media_auth {
    internal;
    proxy_pass http://fastapi/api/media/verify-signature;
    proxy_pass_request_body off;
    proxy_set_header Content-Length "";
    proxy_set_header X-Original-URI $request_uri;
}
```
Make sure the `X-Original-URI` (or `$request_uri`) carries the `stored_name` path plus
the `sig` and `exp` query string so prompt 06's endpoint can verify. If prompt 06
expects different header names, align them here — this config and that endpoint are a
contract.

**`location /health`** → proxy to FastAPI `/health` (or return 200 directly).

### 2. `nginx/nginx.conf` (top-level)

Finalize: `worker_processes auto;`, sensible `worker_connections`, `gzip on` for text
types (not for media), `client_body_timeout`, `keepalive_timeout 65`,
`server_tokens off`, `include /etc/nginx/conf.d/*.conf;`.

### 3. Certbot — `deploy/issue-cert.sh`

A script for **first-time** certificate issuance:
- Run Certbot in **webroot** mode (so Nginx stays up):
  `certbot certonly --webroot -w <webroot> -d family.example.com --email ... --agree-tos
  --non-interactive`.
- The webroot path must match the `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` location in section 1.
  Decide on a host path (e.g. `/var/www/certbot`) and mount it into the Nginx container
  read-only — update `docker-compose.yml` accordingly.
- After issuance, `docker compose exec nginx nginx -s reload`.
- Document the bootstrap chicken-and-egg: the HTTPS `server` block references certs
  that don't exist yet. Solve it by shipping a **bootstrap** `familyapp.conf` that has
  only the port-80 server (serving ACME challenges); issue the cert; then swap in the
  full config and reload. Provide both the bootstrap and full configs, or make the
  HTTPS block conditional. Pick the two-config approach and script the swap.

### 4. Auto-renewal — `deploy/renew-cron`

- A cron entry (or systemd timer) that runs `certbot renew --webroot -w <webroot>
  --deploy-hook "..."` twice daily.
- The deploy hook must (a) reload Nginx and (b) reload Coturn — Coturn shares these
  certs (prompt 09). Reference `coturn/certbot-deploy-hook.sh`.

### 5. Update `docker-compose.yml`

- Mount `/etc/letsencrypt:/etc/letsencrypt:ro` into Nginx (already in prompt 01 —
  confirm).
- Mount the ACME webroot (`/var/www/certbot`) into Nginx.
- Confirm `/var/app-media:/var/app-media:ro` is mounted so `alias /var/app-media/`
  resolves inside the container.

### 6. `deploy/dh-and-headers` (optional hardening)

Optionally generate a DH params file and reference an OCSP stapling resolver. Keep it
optional and documented; don't block the main flow on it.

### 7. Verification doc — `nginx/VERIFY.md`

- `nginx -t` passes inside the container.
- `curl -I http://family.example.com` → 301 to HTTPS.
- `curl https://family.example.com/health` → 200.
- An SSL Labs / `testssl.sh` run shows A/A+ (TLS 1.2/1.3 only).
- A `wscat`/socket.io client connects to `wss://family.example.com/signal/`.
- A signed media URL loads; a tampered one returns 403; a `Range` request returns 206.

## Constraints

- Postgres, Redis, FastAPI, and signaling are **never** exposed on host ports in
  production — only Nginx publishes 80/443.
- TLS 1.0/1.1 disabled; HSTS enabled.
- The media `auth_request` must hit the FastAPI verify endpoint with the original URI
  + query intact.
- Keep `gzip` off for the `/media/` location (already-compressed binaries).

## Acceptance checks

1. `docker compose exec nginx nginx -t` → syntax OK.
2. `deploy/issue-cert.sh` obtains a real certificate for the domain (or a staging cert
   in a test run); Nginx reloads with the full config.
3. `http://` redirects to `https://`; `https://.../health` → 200.
4. `wss://family.example.com/signal/` accepts a Socket.IO connection (prompt 08).
5. A valid signed `/media/...` URL serves the file with `Accept-Ranges: bytes`; a
   tampered signature returns 403.
6. `certbot renew --dry-run` succeeds and the deploy hook reloads Nginx + Coturn.

file.content:
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./backend/api/db:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    networks:
      - app_network
    restart: always

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    command: redis-server /etc/redis/redis.conf
    volumes:
      - ./redis/redis.conf:/etc/redis/redis.conf:ro
      - redis_data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    networks:
      - app_network
    restart: always

  fastapi:
    build: ./backend/api
    env_file: .env
    volumes:
      - media_storage:/app/media
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    expose:
      - "8000"
    networks:
      - app_network
    restart: always

  worker:
    build: ./backend/api
    env_file: .env
    command: ["python", "-m", "app.workers.fcm_worker"]
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - app_network
    restart: always

  signaling:
    build: ./backend/signaling
    env_file: .env
    depends_on:
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    expose:
      - "8001"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8001/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      start_period: 15s
      retries: 3
    networks:
      - app_network
    restart: always

  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
      - ./nginx/conf.d:/etc/nginx/conf.d:ro
      - /etc/letsencrypt:/etc/letsencrypt:ro
      - /var/app-media:/var/app-media:ro
    depends_on:
      - fastapi
      - signaling
    networks:
      - app_network
    restart: always

networks:
  app_network:
    driver: bridge

volumes:
  postgres_data:
  redis_data:
  # In production, override media_storage with a bind mount to /var/app-media
  # via a docker-compose.prod.yml so Nginx can serve files directly.
  media_storage:

# Coturn Verification Guide

## Prerequisites

- `install.sh` has been run and `systemctl status coturn` shows **active (running)**.
- Firewall rules from `firewall.sh --yes` have been applied (ports 3478, 5349, 49152-65535 open).
- DNS for `$DOMAIN` resolves to `$VPS_PUBLIC_IP`.
- TLS certificate exists at `/etc/letsencrypt/live/$DOMAIN/` (prompt 10). Port 5349
  will be down until the cert is issued; all other checks work without it.

---

## 1. Service status

```bash
sudo systemctl status coturn
```

Expected: `active (running)`. If not:
```bash
sudo journalctl -u coturn -n 50 --no-pager
sudo cat /var/log/coturn/turnserver.log
```

---

## 2. STUN smoke test with turnutils_uclient

`turnutils_uclient` is included in the `coturn` package.

```bash
# Plain STUN binding (no auth needed)
turnutils_stunclient $DOMAIN

# TURN allocation with HMAC credentials
# USERNAME format expected by Coturn: "{unix_expiry}:{any_string}"
EXPIRY=$(( $(date +%s) + 3600 ))
USERNAME="${EXPIRY}:smoketest"
# Compute HMAC-SHA1 of username with your TURN_SECRET
CREDENTIAL=$(echo -n "$USERNAME" | openssl dgst -sha1 -hmac "$TURN_SECRET" -binary | base64)

turnutils_uclient \
  -T \
  -u "$USERNAME" \
  -w "$CREDENTIAL" \
  $DOMAIN
```

Expected: allocation succeeds, data relayed, no authentication errors.

---

## 3. TLS / TURNS check (port 5349)

```bash
openssl s_client -connect $DOMAIN:5349 -servername $DOMAIN < /dev/null 2>&1 \
  | grep -E 'Verify|subject|issuer|DONE'
```

Expected: certificate from Let's Encrypt, `Verify return code: 0 (ok)`.

---

## 4. End-to-end relay test with the Trickle-ICE tool

1. Open [https://webrtc.github.io/samples/src/content/peerconnection/trickle-ice/](https://webrtc.github.io/samples/src/content/peerconnection/trickle-ice/)

2. Obtain credentials from the FastAPI server:
   ```bash
   # Register/login first, then:
   curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://$DOMAIN/api/auth/turn-credentials
   ```
   Returns:
   ```json
   {
     "username": "1234567890:userId",
     "credential": "base64string==",
     "ttl": 86400,
     "uris": [
       "stun:family.example.com:3478",
       "turn:family.example.com:3478",
       "turns:family.example.com:5349"
     ]
   }
   ```

3. In the Trickle-ICE tool:
   - Add ICE server: `turn:$DOMAIN:3478`
   - Username: the `username` from the API response
   - Credential: the `credential` from the API response
   - Click **Gather candidates**

4. Expected output: at least one candidate with type **`relay`** appears.
   If only `host` and `srflx` appear, TURN relay is blocked — check the firewall.

---

## 5. Log monitoring during a test call

```bash
tail -f /var/log/coturn/turnserver.log
```

During a call you should see allocation requests, permission grants, and data
channel activity. No `ERROR` or `auth failed` lines should appear.

---

## 6. Certificate renewal verification

After a cert renewal (manual or automatic):

```bash
# Simulate renewal
sudo certbot renew --dry-run

# Or trigger the deploy hook directly
sudo /etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/reload-coturn.sh

# Confirm Coturn reloaded without restarting
sudo systemctl status coturn
# Should still show the original start time, not a new one
```

---

## Certificate dependency note

`install.sh` should be run **after** `certbot certonly` has issued the certificate.
If you install Coturn before the cert exists:
- Coturn starts successfully on port 3478 (STUN/TURN over UDP/TCP).
- Port 5349 (TURNS/TLS) will **not** open until the cert files exist.
- Once the cert is issued, `sudo systemctl restart coturn` will bring 5349 up.
- Going forward, the `certbot-deploy-hook.sh` keeps the cert fresh automatically.

---

## Common issues

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Authentication failed` | `TURN_SECRET` mismatch between Coturn and FastAPI | Verify both use same `TURN_SECRET` from `.env` |
| No `relay` candidate | UDP 49152-65535 blocked | Re-run `firewall.sh --yes`, check DO Cloud Firewall |
| Port 5349 refused | Cert not yet issued | Run `certbot certonly` first (prompt 10) |
| Coturn won't start | Config syntax error | `sudo turnserver -c /etc/turnserver.conf --check` |
| `lt-cred-mech` conflict | Old config leftover | Remove `lt-cred-mech` from `/etc/turnserver.conf` |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# coturn/certbot-deploy-hook.sh
#
# Certbot deploy hook — reload Coturn after a certificate renewal so it picks
# up the new cert/key without a full restart (no call interruption).
#
# Installation:
#   sudo cp coturn/certbot-deploy-hook.sh \
#        /etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/reload-coturn.sh
#   sudo chmod +x /etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/reload-coturn.sh
#
# Certbot runs all executable files in renewal-hooks/deploy/ after a successful
# renewal. This hook is also referenced by the Nginx prompt (prompt 10).
#
# Test manually (simulates a renewal):
#   sudo certbot renew --dry-run
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

if systemctl is-active --quiet coturn; then
  echo "Reloading Coturn to pick up renewed certificate..."
  systemctl reload coturn
  echo "Coturn reloaded successfully."
else
  echo "Coturn is not running — skipping reload."
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# coturn/firewall.sh — Open required ports for Coturn with ufw
#
# Usage:
#   sudo bash coturn/firewall.sh --yes
#
# Without --yes the script prints what it would do and exits (dry-run).
#
# Required ports:
#   UDP 3478          STUN / TURN (plain)
#   TCP 3478          TURN over TCP (firewall traversal)
#   TCP 5349          TURNS / TLS
#   UDP 49152-65535   TURN media relay
#
# Ports this script NEVER touches (preserved):
#   TCP 22   SSH
#   TCP 80   HTTP (Nginx / certbot)
#   TCP 443  HTTPS (Nginx)
#
# DigitalOcean Cloud Firewall equivalent rules (manage in the DO dashboard
# or via doctl / Terraform — these are NOT applied by this script):
#
#   Inbound rules:
#     Protocol  Port(s)         Sources
#     UDP       3478            All IPv4, All IPv6
#     TCP       3478            All IPv4, All IPv6
#     TCP       5349            All IPv4, All IPv6
#     UDP       49152-65535     All IPv4, All IPv6
#     TCP       22              (restrict to your IPs in production)
#     TCP       80              All IPv4, All IPv6
#     TCP       443             All IPv4, All IPv6
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

APPLY=false

for arg in "$@"; do
  if [[ "$arg" == "--yes" ]]; then
    APPLY=true
  fi
done

# ── Dry-run notice ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ "$APPLY" != true ]]; then
  echo "DRY RUN — no changes will be made."
  echo "Re-run with --yes to apply."
  echo ""
  echo "Would execute the following ufw commands:"
  echo "  ufw allow 22/tcp        # SSH (ensure not dropped)"
  echo "  ufw allow 80/tcp        # HTTP"
  echo "  ufw allow 443/tcp       # HTTPS"
  echo "  ufw allow 3478/udp      # STUN / TURN"
  echo "  ufw allow 3478/tcp      # TURN over TCP"
  echo "  ufw allow 5349/tcp      # TURNS / TLS"
  echo "  ufw allow 49152:65535/udp  # TURN media relay"
  echo ""
  echo "WARNING: Applying firewall rules can lock you out if SSH is not open."
  echo "Verify 'ufw status' before enabling if ufw is not yet active."
  exit 0
fi

# ── Safety check ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "==> Ensuring SSH (TCP 22) is allowed before any changes..."
ufw allow 22/tcp comment "SSH"

echo "==> Ensuring HTTP/HTTPS are allowed..."
ufw allow 80/tcp  comment "HTTP"
ufw allow 443/tcp comment "HTTPS"

echo "==> Opening Coturn ports..."
ufw allow 3478/udp comment "STUN/TURN"
ufw allow 3478/tcp comment "TURN-TCP"
ufw allow 5349/tcp comment "TURNS-TLS"
ufw allow 49152:65535/udp comment "TURN-relay"

echo "==> Enabling ufw (if not already active)..."
# 'ufw --force enable' is idempotent and won't drop existing connections
ufw --force enable

echo ""
echo "==> Current ufw status:"
ufw status verbose

echo ""
echo "================================================================"
echo " Firewall rules applied successfully."
echo " SSH (TCP 22) is open — you are not locked out."
echo "================================================================"
echo ""
echo "REMINDER: If you use DigitalOcean Cloud Firewall, also add the"
echo "equivalent inbound rules in the DO dashboard (see comments at the"
echo "top of this script). ufw and DO Cloud Firewall operate independently."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# coturn/install.sh — Idempotent Coturn install and configuration
#
# Usage:
#   export VPS_PUBLIC_IP=1.2.3.4
#   export DOMAIN=family.example.com
#   export TURN_SECRET=your-secret-here
#   sudo -E bash coturn/install.sh
#
# Or pass variables as arguments:
#   sudo bash coturn/install.sh 1.2.3.4 family.example.com your-secret
#
# Safe to re-run — each step is checked before executing.
# Run AFTER certbot has issued the certificate (see verify.md); Coturn starts
# without TLS (port 5349 down) if the cert files do not exist yet.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

# ── Argument / env handling ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
VPS_PUBLIC_IP="${1:-${VPS_PUBLIC_IP:-}}"
DOMAIN="${2:-${DOMAIN:-}}"
TURN_SECRET="${3:-${TURN_SECRET:-}}"

if [[ -z "$TURN_SECRET" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: TURN_SECRET is required." >&2
  echo "  export TURN_SECRET=<secret>  OR  pass as third argument." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ -z "$VPS_PUBLIC_IP" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: VPS_PUBLIC_IP is required." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ -z "$DOMAIN" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: DOMAIN is required." >&2
  exit 1
fi

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
CONF_TEMPLATE="$SCRIPT_DIR/turnserver.conf"
COTURN_CONF="/etc/turnserver.conf"
COTURN_DEFAULT="/etc/default/coturn"
LOG_DIR="/var/log/coturn"

echo "==> Installing Coturn..."
if dpkg -s coturn &>/dev/null; then
  echo "    coturn already installed, skipping apt."
else
  apt-get update -qq
  apt-get install -y coturn
fi

echo "==> Enabling Coturn service in $COTURN_DEFAULT..."
if grep -qE '^TURNSERVER_ENABLED=1' "$COTURN_DEFAULT" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "    Already enabled."
else
  # Replace or append the directive
  if grep -qE '^#?TURNSERVER_ENABLED' "$COTURN_DEFAULT" 2>/dev/null; then
    sed -i 's/^#*TURNSERVER_ENABLED.*/TURNSERVER_ENABLED=1/' "$COTURN_DEFAULT"
  else
    echo "TURNSERVER_ENABLED=1" >> "$COTURN_DEFAULT"
  fi
fi

echo "==> Creating log directory $LOG_DIR..."
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
chown -R turnserver:turnserver "$LOG_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Writing $COTURN_CONF from template..."
if [[ ! -f "$CONF_TEMPLATE" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: Template not found at $CONF_TEMPLATE" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Substitute placeholders using sed (avoids envsubst dependency)
sed \
  -e "s|\${VPS_PUBLIC_IP}|$VPS_PUBLIC_IP|g" \
  -e "s|\${DOMAIN}|$DOMAIN|g" \
  -e "s|\${TURN_SECRET}|$TURN_SECRET|g" \
  "$CONF_TEMPLATE" > "$COTURN_CONF"

chmod 640 "$COTURN_CONF"
chown root:turnserver "$COTURN_CONF" 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Verifying substitution (no placeholders should remain)..."
if grep -qE '\$\{(VPS_PUBLIC_IP|DOMAIN|TURN_SECRET)\}' "$COTURN_CONF"; then
  echo "ERROR: Unresolved placeholders in $COTURN_CONF" >&2
  grep -E '\$\{' "$COTURN_CONF" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "==> Enabling and restarting Coturn..."
systemctl enable coturn
systemctl restart coturn

echo ""
echo "================================================================"
echo " Coturn installed successfully."
echo "================================================================"
echo ""
echo "Verification steps:"
echo "  1. Check service status:"
echo "       sudo systemctl status coturn"
echo ""
echo "  2. STUN smoke test (install: apt install coturn):"
echo "       turnutils_uclient -T $VPS_PUBLIC_IP"
echo ""
echo "  3. TLS check (requires cert — see verify.md):"
echo "       openssl s_client -connect $DOMAIN:5349 -servername $DOMAIN"
echo ""
echo "  4. Full relay test:"
echo "       See coturn/verify.md for the Trickle-ICE web tool instructions."
echo ""
echo "  5. Watch logs:"
echo "       tail -f $LOG_DIR/turnserver.log"
echo ""
echo "NOTE: If /etc/letsencrypt/live/$DOMAIN/ does not exist yet,"
echo "      port 5349 (TLS) will be down until certs are issued (prompt 10)."
echo "      After cert renewal, run:"
echo "       sudo systemctl reload coturn"
echo "      or install coturn/certbot-deploy-hook.sh to do it automatically."

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./backend/api/db:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    networks:
      - app_network
    restart: always

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    command: redis-server /etc/redis/redis.conf
    volumes:
      - ./redis/redis.conf:/etc/redis/redis.conf:ro
      - redis_data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    networks:
      - app_network
    restart: always

  fastapi:
    build: ./backend/api
    env_file: .env
    volumes:
      - media_storage:/app/media
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    expose:
      - "8000"
    networks:
      - app_network
    restart: always

  worker:
    build: ./backend/api
    env_file: .env
    command: ["python", "-m", "app.workers.fcm_worker"]
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - app_network
    restart: always

  signaling:
    build: ./backend/signaling
    env_file: .env
    depends_on:
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    expose:
      - "8001"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8001/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      start_period: 15s
      retries: 3
    networks:
      - app_network
    restart: always

  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
      - ./nginx/conf.d:/etc/nginx/conf.d:ro
      - /etc/letsencrypt:/etc/letsencrypt:ro
      - /var/app-media:/var/app-media:ro
    depends_on:
      - fastapi
      - signaling
    networks:
      - app_network
    restart: always

networks:
  app_network:
    driver: bridge

volumes:
  postgres_data:
  redis_data:
  # In production, override media_storage with a bind mount to /var/app-media
  # via a docker-compose.prod.yml so Nginx can serve files directly.
  media_storage:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# deploy/issue-cert.sh — First-time TLS cert issuance and nginx SSL activation
#
# Usage (run as root on the VPS from the project directory):
#   export DOMAIN=family.example.com
#   export EMAIL=admin@example.com
#   sudo -E bash deploy/issue-cert.sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Issues a Let's Encrypt cert via certbot webroot challenge
#   2. Substitutes ${DOMAIN} in nginx/ssl.conf.template
#   3. Writes the resolved config to nginx/conf.d/familyapp.conf
#   4. Tests and reloads nginx
#   5. Installs a certbot deploy hook that reloads nginx on every renewal
#
# Prerequisites:
#   - certbot installed: sudo apt-get install -y certbot
#   - Docker Compose stack running with bootstrap config:
#       docker compose up -d
#   - DNS for $DOMAIN pointing to this server's public IP
#   - Port 80 open and reachable from the internet (ACME challenge)
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

DOMAIN="${DOMAIN:-}"
EMAIL="${EMAIL:-}"

if [[ -z "$DOMAIN" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: DOMAIN is required." >&2
  echo "  export DOMAIN=family.example.com" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ -z "$EMAIL" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: EMAIL is required for Let's Encrypt registration." >&2
  echo "  export EMAIL=admin@example.com" >&2
  exit 1
fi

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
CONF_TEMPLATE="$PROJECT_ROOT/nginx/ssl.conf.template"
CONF_DEST="$PROJECT_ROOT/nginx/conf.d/familyapp.conf"
WEBROOT="/var/www/certbot"
COMPOSE="docker compose -f $PROJECT_ROOT/docker-compose.yml"

# ── 1. Sanity checks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

if ! command -v certbot &>/dev/null; then
  echo "ERROR: certbot not found." >&2
  echo "  sudo apt-get install -y certbot" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if ! command -v docker &>/dev/null; then
  echo "ERROR: docker not found." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -f "$CONF_TEMPLATE" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: SSL template not found at $CONF_TEMPLATE" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# ── 2. Webroot directory ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

echo "==> Creating ACME webroot $WEBROOT..."
mkdir -p "$WEBROOT"

# ── 3. Verify nginx bootstrap config is valid and running ────────────────────

echo "==> Verifying nginx bootstrap config..."
if ! $COMPOSE exec -T nginx nginx -t; then
  echo "ERROR: nginx config test failed. Fix the config before continuing." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "==> Checking nginx is responding on port 80..."
if ! curl -fsS --max-time 5 "http://localhost/health" &>/dev/null; then
  echo "WARNING: /health is not responding on localhost:80." >&2
  echo "  Ensure the stack is running: docker compose up -d" >&2
fi

# ── 4. Issue certificate ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

echo "==> Requesting Let's Encrypt certificate for $DOMAIN..."
certbot certonly \
  --webroot \
  --webroot-path "$WEBROOT" \
  --non-interactive \
  --agree-tos \
  --email "$EMAIL" \
  --domain "$DOMAIN" \
  --rsa-key-size 4096

echo "==> Certificate issued: /etc/letsencrypt/live/$DOMAIN/"

# ── 5. Generate SSL nginx config from template ───────────────────────────────

echo "==> Generating SSL nginx config..."
sed "s|\${DOMAIN}|$DOMAIN|g" "$CONF_TEMPLATE" > "$CONF_DEST"

echo "    Written: $CONF_DEST"

# ── 6. Verify resolved config has no remaining placeholders ──────────────────

if grep -q '\${DOMAIN}' "$CONF_DEST"; then
  echo "ERROR: Unresolved placeholders remain in $CONF_DEST" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# ── 7. Test and reload nginx ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

echo "==> Testing nginx SSL config..."
$COMPOSE exec -T nginx nginx -t

echo "==> Reloading nginx..."
$COMPOSE exec -T nginx nginx -s reload

# ── 8. Install certbot deploy hook for automatic renewals ────────────────────

HOOK_DIR="/etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy"
HOOK_FILE="$HOOK_DIR/reload-nginx.sh"

echo "==> Installing certbot renewal deploy hook at $HOOK_FILE..."
mkdir -p "$HOOK_DIR"
cat > "$HOOK_FILE" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reload nginx after certbot renews the certificate (no downtime).
docker compose -f $PROJECT_ROOT/docker-compose.yml exec -T nginx nginx -s reload
EOF
chmod +x "$HOOK_FILE"

echo ""
echo "================================================================"
echo " TLS certificate issued — nginx is now serving HTTPS."
echo "================================================================"
echo ""
echo "  Domain  : https://$DOMAIN"
echo "  Cert    : /etc/letsencrypt/live/$DOMAIN/"
echo "  Hook    : $HOOK_FILE"
echo ""
echo "Next steps:"
echo ""
echo "  1. Install the auto-renewal cron job:"
echo "       sudo cp $SCRIPT_DIR/renew-cron /etc/cron.d/familylink-certbot"
echo "       sudo chmod 644 /etc/cron.d/familylink-certbot"
echo ""
echo "  2. (Optional) Harden TLS with Diffie-Hellman parameters:"
echo "       sudo bash $SCRIPT_DIR/dh-and-headers.sh"
echo ""
echo "  3. Verify TLS:"
echo "       curl -I https://$DOMAIN/health"
echo "       openssl s_client -connect $DOMAIN:443 -servername $DOMAIN < /dev/null"
echo ""
echo "  4. Full verification checklist: nginx/VERIFY.md"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# deploy/dh-and-headers.sh — Optional TLS hardening: Diffie-Hellman parameters
#
# Generates a 2048-bit DH params file and activates it inside the running
# nginx container. Adds the ssl_dhparam directive to the live nginx config.
#
# Usage (run as root after deploy/issue-cert.sh):
#   sudo bash deploy/dh-and-headers.sh
#
# The DH params are stored inside the container at /etc/nginx/dhparam.pem.
# They survive nginx reloads but are lost on container restart — re-run this
# script after container recreation (e.g., after 'docker compose up -d --build').
#
# Why: TLS 1.3 uses ECDHE exclusively (no DHE), so DHE params only matter for
# TLS 1.2 clients. Modern clients use TLS 1.3; this is belt-and-suspenders.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
CONF_FILE="$PROJECT_ROOT/nginx/conf.d/familyapp.conf"
COMPOSE="docker compose -f $PROJECT_ROOT/docker-compose.yml"

# ── Check prerequisites ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

if [[ ! -f "$CONF_FILE" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: $CONF_FILE not found. Run deploy/issue-cert.sh first." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if ! $COMPOSE exec -T nginx true &>/dev/null; then
  echo "ERROR: nginx container is not running." >&2
  echo "  docker compose up -d" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# ── Generate DH params ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

TMPFILE="$(mktemp /tmp/dhparam.XXXXXX.pem)"
trap 'rm -f "$TMPFILE"' EXIT

echo "==> Generating 2048-bit DH parameters (this may take a minute)..."
openssl dhparam -out "$TMPFILE" 2048

echo "==> Copying DH params into nginx container..."
NGINX_CONTAINER=$($COMPOSE ps -q nginx)
docker cp "$TMPFILE" "$NGINX_CONTAINER:/etc/nginx/dhparam.pem"

# ── Patch nginx config ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

echo "==> Patching $CONF_FILE to add ssl_dhparam directive..."

if grep -q 'ssl_dhparam' "$CONF_FILE"; then
  echo "    ssl_dhparam already present — skipping patch."
else
  # Insert after ssl_session_tickets line
  sed -i 's|ssl_session_tickets.*off;|&\n    ssl_dhparam          /etc/nginx/dhparam.pem;|' "$CONF_FILE"
  echo "    ssl_dhparam directive added."
fi

# ── Test and reload ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

echo "==> Testing nginx config..."
$COMPOSE exec -T nginx nginx -t

echo "==> Reloading nginx..."
$COMPOSE exec -T nginx nginx -s reload

echo ""
echo "================================================================"
echo " DH parameters active. nginx reloaded."
echo "================================================================"
echo ""
echo "NOTE: DH params live inside the container and are lost on restart."
echo "Re-run this script after 'docker compose up -d --build' or similar."
echo ""
echo "Verify DHE in use:"
echo "  openssl s_client -connect \$DOMAIN:443 -cipher DHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 < /dev/null"

# Nginx Verification Guide

## Prerequisites

- Docker Compose stack is running: `docker compose up -d`
- `$DOMAIN` DNS resolves to the server's public IP
- Port 80 and 443 are open

---

## 1. Bootstrap config (before TLS cert)

### nginx starts cleanly

```bash
docker compose exec nginx nginx -t
# Expected: syntax is ok / test is successful

docker compose ps nginx
# Expected: Up
```

### ACME challenge directory is accessible

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /var/www/certbot
echo "test" | sudo tee /var/www/certbot/.well-known/acme-challenge/probe
curl http://$DOMAIN/.well-known/acme-challenge/probe
# Expected: test
sudo rm -f /var/www/certbot/.well-known/acme-challenge/probe
```

### Health endpoint

```bash
curl http://$DOMAIN/health
# Expected: {"status":"ok"} or similar from FastAPI
```

---

## 2. Issue TLS certificate

```bash
export DOMAIN=family.example.com
export EMAIL=admin@example.com
sudo -E bash deploy/issue-cert.sh
```

Expected output ends with "TLS certificate issued — nginx is now serving HTTPS."

---

## 3. TLS verification

### HTTPS health check

```bash
curl -I https://$DOMAIN/health
# Expected: HTTP/2 200
```

### Certificate details

```bash
openssl s_client -connect $DOMAIN:443 -servername $DOMAIN < /dev/null 2>&1 \
  | grep -E 'subject|issuer|Verify|Protocol|Cipher'
# Expected:
#   subject=/CN=family.example.com
#   issuer=Let's Encrypt
#   Verify return code: 0 (ok)
#   Protocol: TLSv1.3 (or TLSv1.2)
```

### HTTP → HTTPS redirect

```bash
curl -I http://$DOMAIN/api/auth/login
# Expected: HTTP/1.1 301 and Location: https://...
```

### SSL Labs grade (optional, external tool)

Open: https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/analyze.html?d=$DOMAIN
Expected: A or A+

---

## 4. Security headers

```bash
curl -sI https://$DOMAIN/health | grep -iE \
  'strict-transport|x-content-type|x-frame|referrer|permissions'
# Expected all five headers present
```

---

## 5. API proxy

```bash
curl -s https://$DOMAIN/health
# Expected: FastAPI health response

curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://$DOMAIN/api/auth/login \
  -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{}'
# Expected: 422 (validation error from FastAPI, not nginx 502)
```

---

## 6. Signaling WebSocket

Using a browser or wscat:

```bash
npm install -g wscat
wscat -c "wss://$DOMAIN/signal?EIO=4&transport=websocket" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
# Expected: connects (101 Upgrade), then Socket.IO handshake payload
```

### Signaling health (external endpoint)

```bash
curl -s https://$DOMAIN/signal/health
# Expected: {"status":"ok"}
```

---

## 7. Auto-renewal

### Install cron and test

```bash
sudo cp deploy/renew-cron /etc/cron.d/familylink-certbot
sudo chmod 644 /etc/cron.d/familylink-certbot

# Simulate a renewal (no actual renewal if cert is fresh)
sudo certbot renew --dry-run
# Expected: Congratulations, all simulated renewals succeeded / no changes needed
```

### Verify deploy hook is installed

```bash
cat /etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/reload-nginx.sh
# Expected: contains 'docker compose ... nginx -s reload'

sudo bash /etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/reload-nginx.sh
# Expected: nginx reload succeeds (no error output)
```

---

## 8. Log monitoring

```bash
docker compose logs -f nginx
```

During normal operation:
- Access log lines for each request
- No `upstream connect error` lines

Possible issues:

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `502 Bad Gateway` | Upstream container not running | `docker compose ps`, check service health |
| `SSL_ERROR_RX_RECORD_TOO_LONG` | Port 443 serving HTTP | Check `listen 443 ssl` in config |
| `curl: (60) SSL cert not OK` | Cert not yet issued | Run `deploy/issue-cert.sh` |
| `/health` returns 404 | FastAPI health route missing | Check `GET /health` in FastAPI |
| WebSocket 400 | Hitting `/signal/health` as WS | Use `/signal` for socket, `/signal/health` for HTTP |
| `auth_request` 500 | `/api/media/auth` endpoint missing | Implement media auth route in FastAPI |

112	A thin wrapper over `flutter_secure_storage`:
113	- `saveRefreshToken / readRefreshToken / deleteRefreshToken`.

115	  persist it (used by auth + refresh).

118

120	- `MessagesTable`: id (text PK), conversationId, senderId, messageType, content
121	  (nullable), mediaLocalPath (nullable), mediaRemoteUrl (nullable),
122	  thumbnailUrl (nullable), status (default 'sent'), replyToId (nullable),

128	  durationSeconds (nullable).

130	  uploadedBytes, totalBytes, status — for resumable uploads (used in prompt 13).
131	
132	Enable WAL mode. Provide DAOs as separate classes (`MessagesDao`, `ConversationsDao`,
133	etc.) with the basic CRUD + an `upsert`/`insertOrReplace` for messages (idempotent on
134	`id`). Wire `drift_dev` code generation (`part 'local_db.g.dart';`).
135

137	
138	- `dio_client.dart`: a `Dio` configured with `AppConfig.apiBaseUrl`, JSON content type,
139	  connect/receive timeouts, and the interceptors below.
140	- `token_interceptor.dart`:
141	  - **Request**: attach `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` from the in-memory auth
142	    state (accessToken lives in Riverpod state, never on disk).
143	  - **Response/Error**: on `401`, attempt a single token refresh:
144	    - Call `POST /api/auth/refresh` with the stored refresh token + device id.
145	    - Use a lock/mutex so concurrent 401s trigger only **one** refresh; queue the
146	      other requests and replay them after.
147	    - On refresh success: update the in-memory access token + persist the rotated
148	      refresh token, retry the original request.
149	    - On refresh failure: clear tokens, push the app to the login route.

151	  online/offline that Riverpod can watch.

155	A clean Material 3 light + dark theme. Family-app friendly: large tap targets,
156	readable text sizes (some users may be older relatives — bias toward larger defaults).
157

159	
160	- `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()`, `Firebase.initializeApp()`.
161	- Register a **top-level** `firebaseMessagingBackgroundHandler` (must be a top-level or
162	  static function with `@pragma('vm:entry-point')`) — for now it just logs; prompt 15
163	  expands it for call wakeup.
164	- Request notification permission (`firebase_messaging` + `permission_handler`).
165	- Wrap the app in `ProviderScope`.
166

168	
169	- `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` — add all permissions and service
170	  declarations the app will need (the calling features in prompt 15 rely on these,
171	  declare them now):
172	  - Permissions: `INTERNET`, `RECORD_AUDIO`, `CAMERA`, `MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS`,
173	    `WAKE_LOCK`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_PHONE_CALL`,
174	    `USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT`, `VIBRATE`, `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED`,
175	    `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`, `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES`, `READ_MEDIA_VIDEO`, `READ_MEDIA_AUDIO`.
176	  - Placeholder `<service>` entries for `.CallService`
177	    (`foregroundServiceType="phoneCall|microphone|camera"`) and `.FcmService` — the
178	    Kotlin classes are written in prompt 15; declare the services now with a TODO.
179	- `android/app/build.gradle` — set `minSdkVersion 24`, `targetSdkVersion 34`, enable
180	  core library desugaring (needed by `flutter_local_notifications`), apply the
181	  `com.google.gms.google-services` plugin.
182	- `android/build.gradle` — add the Google Services classpath.
183	- Add a placeholder `google-services.json` location note (the real file is added by
184	  the developer from the Firebase console; it is gitignored).
185	
186	### 11. Notification channels — `core/services/notification_service.dart` (partial)
187	
188	Create the service with channel setup only (full logic in prompts 13/15):
189	- Initialize `flutter_local_notifications`.
190	- Create two Android channels: `messages` (default importance, sound) and `calls`
191	  (max importance, full-screen-intent capable, custom ringtone, vibration). Leave a
192	  TODO for showing notifications.
193	
194	### 12. Routing — `app.dart`
195	
196	`go_router` with routes: `/splash`, `/login`, `/register`, `/otp`, `/home`,
197	`/chat/:conversationId`, `/call/incoming`, `/call/active`, `/contacts`, `/profile`.

199	based on auth state sends unauthenticated users to `/login` (auth state provider is
200	built in prompt 12 — leave a clearly marked hook).

204	Run `dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` so Drift and Riverpod

223	5. The Drift DB file is created on first run; a quick insert/read of a `Message` works.
224	6. Both Android notification channels (`messages`, `calls`) appear in system settings.

The code is perfectly fine — `flutter analyze` shows **zero issues** and `build_runner` generates all files successfully. The APK build failure is **100% an environment problem**, not a code problem.

Here's exactly what's happening:

**Root cause:** Gradle 8.14 (which Flutter 3.38.9 auto-generates) uses Java 17's `WEPollSelectorImpl` for its daemon IPC — this requires **AF_UNIX (Unix domain) socket** support. The Claude Code sandbox environment blocks AF_UNIX socket connections at the OS level, so Gradle dies immediately before it even tries to compile your code:

```
java.net.SocketException: Invalid argument: connect
  ↳ sun.nio.ch.UnixDomainSockets.connect0  ← blocked by sandbox
  ↳ WEPollSelectorImpl.<init>
  ↳ Gradle daemon startup fails
```

**What this means for you:**

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `flutter pub get` | ✅ Works |
| `dart run build_runner build` | ✅ Works (140 outputs) |
| `flutter analyze` | ✅ Zero issues |
| `flutter build apk` on **your machine** | ✅ Will work |
| `flutter build apk` in **this sandbox** | ❌ Java/Gradle blocked |

**To build the APK yourself** — run this on your dev machine:

```bash
cd calling-app/familylink/flutter_app

# Replace the placeholder google-services.json first:
# Copy your real file from Firebase Console → Project Settings → Android app
# → android/app/google-services.json

flutter build apk --debug \
  --dart-define=API_BASE_URL=https://family.example.com \
  --dart-define=SIGNALING_URL=wss://family.example.com
```

The APK will be at `build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-debug.apk`. Ready to move on to prompt 12?

# Prompt 12 — Flutter Auth & Contacts

Implement the FamilyLink authentication flow (register → OTP → login), auth state
management, auto-login, and the contacts + profile features. Work in `flutter_app/`.
Depends on prompt 11 (foundation) and backend prompts 03, 04.

## Goal

A user can register, verify an OTP, log in, stay logged in across restarts (auto-login
via refresh token), see and add family contacts, and edit their profile + avatar.

## Tasks

### 1. Feature folders

Create:
```
lib/features/auth/
  data/auth_repository.dart
  domain/auth_notifier.dart
  domain/auth_state.dart
  presentation/login_screen.dart
  presentation/register_screen.dart
  presentation/otp_screen.dart
  presentation/splash_screen.dart
lib/features/contacts/
  data/contact_repository.dart
  domain/contacts_notifier.dart
  presentation/contacts_screen.dart
  presentation/add_contact_screen.dart
lib/features/profile/
  data/profile_repository.dart
  presentation/profile_screen.dart
```

### 2. `auth_repository.dart`

Methods calling the FastAPI auth endpoints via the Dio client:
- `register({name, phone, password})` → `POST /api/auth/register`.
- `verifyOtp({phone, otp})` → `POST /api/auth/verify-otp` → returns tokens.
- `login({phone, password})` → `POST /api/auth/login` (include `device_id` from
  `SecureStorage`, and the current FCM token).
- `logout()` → `POST /api/auth/logout` with the refresh token.
- `getMe()` → `GET /api/users/me`.

On any call that returns tokens: persist the refresh token + device id via
`SecureStorage`, return the access token + user to the caller (the notifier holds the
access token in memory).

### 3. `auth_state.dart` + `auth_notifier.dart`

- `AuthState`: a sealed/union — `Unknown` (app start, checking), `Unauthenticated`,
  `Authenticating`, `Authenticated(User user, String accessToken)`,
  `AuthError(String message)`. Also a transient `OtpPending(String phone)` state.
- `AuthNotifier` (Riverpod `Notifier`/`StateNotifier`):
  - `bootstrap()` — called on splash: if a refresh token exists, call
    `POST /api/auth/refresh`; on success fetch `getMe()` and become `Authenticated`,
    else `Unauthenticated`.
  - `register(...)` → on success → `OtpPending`.
  - `verifyOtp(...)` → on success → `Authenticated`.
  - `login(...)` → `Authenticating` → `Authenticated` / `AuthError`.
  - `logout()` → call repo, clear secure storage, become `Unauthenticated`.
  - Expose the current access token to the Dio interceptor (prompt 11) — the
    interceptor reads from this provider; on a successful refresh inside the
    interceptor, it must update this state.
- Expose `authStateProvider`.

### 4. Wire the router redirect (from prompt 11)

`go_router`'s `redirect` now consults `authStateProvider`:
- `Unknown` → stay on `/splash`.
- `Unauthenticated` / `AuthError` → `/login`.
- `OtpPending` → `/otp`.
- `Authenticated` → `/home` (if currently on an auth route).

### 5. Screens

- **Splash** (`/splash`): on mount calls `AuthNotifier.bootstrap()`; shows the logo +
  spinner; the router moves it onward.
- **Login** (`/login`): phone + password fields, validation, "Log in" button (loading
  state), link to Register. Phone field uses a sensible keyboard type.
- **Register** (`/register`): name + phone + password + confirm; client-side validation
  (password ≥ 8 chars, phone format). On submit → `AuthNotifier.register`.
- **OTP** (`/otp`): 6-digit code entry (use a segmented/boxed input), a resend button
  with a cooldown timer, shows the phone being verified. In debug builds, if the
  register response included `debug_otp`, pre-fill it and show a "debug" hint.
- All screens: friendly error display via the shared `error_snackbar`; large,
  accessible controls (older relatives may use this app).

### 6. `contact_repository.dart`

- `listContacts()` → `GET /api/contacts`.
- `addContact({phone, nickname})` → `POST /api/contacts`.
- `removeContact(contactId)` → `DELETE /api/contacts/{id}`.
- Cache contacts into the Drift `UsersTable` for offline display.

### 7. `contacts_notifier.dart` + screens

- `ContactsNotifier` loads contacts (from Drift first for instant render, then
  refreshes from the API), exposes `AsyncValue<List<Contact>>`.
- **Contacts screen** (`/contacts`): list of family members with avatar, name,
  presence dot (presence wiring comes in prompt 13 — leave the dot wired to a
  placeholder provider). Tapping a contact opens/creates a chat (routes to
  `/chat/:conversationId` — conversation creation happens on first message in
  prompt 13; for now pass the contact's user id).
- **Add contact screen**: phone input + optional nickname, submit, handle "user not
  found" and "already a contact" errors gracefully.

### 8. `profile_repository.dart` + profile screen

- `updateProfile({name})` → `PUT /api/users/me`.
- `uploadAvatar(File image)` → `POST /api/users/avatar` (multipart).
- `registerFcmToken(token)` → `POST /api/users/fcm-token` — call this after login and
  whenever FCM issues a new token (`onTokenRefresh`).
- **Profile screen** (`/profile`): show name, phone, avatar; edit name; pick + upload a
  new avatar via `image_picker`; a "Log out" button; a section linking to battery-
  optimization settings (used heavily in prompt 15 — stub the button now).

### 9. FCM token registration

After a successful login/OTP verification, fetch the FCM token
(`FirebaseMessaging.instance.getToken()`) and call `registerFcmToken`. Subscribe to
`FirebaseMessaging.instance.onTokenRefresh` and re-register on change.

### 10. Tests — `flutter_app/test/`

- Unit-test `AuthNotifier`: bootstrap with/without a stored refresh token, login
  success/failure, otp flow, logout clears storage. Mock the repository.
- Unit-test `ContactsNotifier`: loads from cache then refreshes.

## Constraints

- Access token only in memory (the notifier); refresh token only in secure storage.
- The router redirect is the single source of navigation truth — screens don't
  navigate imperatively for auth transitions.
- All network errors surface as friendly messages, never raw exceptions.

## Acceptance checks

1. Fresh install → splash → login. Register a new user → OTP screen → enter the code
   (debug OTP shown in debug builds) → lands on `/home`.
2. Kill and relaunch the app → auto-login via refresh token → straight to `/home`.
3. Log out → returns to `/login`; relaunch stays on `/login`.
4. Add a family member by phone → appears in the contacts list; adding an unknown
   number shows a clear error.
5. Edit the profile name and upload an avatar → both persist (verify via `GET /me`).
6. `flutter test` passes for the auth and contacts notifiers.

abstract final class AppTheme {
  // ── Typography (generous sizes for older family members) ──────────────────
  static const _textTheme = TextTheme(
    bodySmall:      TextStyle(fontSize: 13),
    bodyMedium:     TextStyle(fontSize: 15),
    bodyLarge:      TextStyle(fontSize: 17),
    titleSmall:     TextStyle(fontSize: 15, fontWeight: FontWeight.w600),

    headlineLarge:  TextStyle(fontSize: 32, fontWeight: FontWeight.w600),
  );

  // ── Shared input decoration (18 px radius, floating label) ────────────────
  static InputDecorationTheme _inputTheme(Color fill) => InputDecorationTheme(
        filled: true,
        fillColor: fill,
        floatingLabelBehavior: FloatingLabelBehavior.auto,
        contentPadding:
            const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 20, vertical: 20),
        border: OutlineInputBorder(
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(18),
          borderSide: BorderSide.none,
        ),
        enabledBorder: OutlineInputBorder(
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(18),
          borderSide: BorderSide.none,
        ),
        focusedBorder: OutlineInputBorder(
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(18),
          borderSide:
              const BorderSide(color: AppColors.primary, width: 2),
        ),
        errorBorder: OutlineInputBorder(
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(18),
          borderSide:
              const BorderSide(color: AppColors.danger, width: 1.5),
        ),
        focusedErrorBorder: OutlineInputBorder(
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(18),
          borderSide:
              const BorderSide(color: AppColors.danger, width: 2),
        ),
        labelStyle: const TextStyle(fontSize: 15),
        errorStyle: const TextStyle(color: AppColors.danger, fontSize: 12),
      );

  // ── Pill button (56 px tall, stadium shape) ───────────────────────────────
  static final _elevatedButton = ElevatedButtonThemeData(
    style: ElevatedButton.styleFrom(
      minimumSize: const Size(double.infinity, 56),
      shape: const StadiumBorder(),
      backgroundColor: AppColors.primary,
      foregroundColor: Colors.white,
      disabledBackgroundColor: AppColors.primary.withAlpha(100),
      textStyle: const TextStyle(
        fontSize: 17,
        fontWeight: FontWeight.w600,
        letterSpacing: 0.3,
      ),
      elevation: 0,
    ),
  );

  // ── Light theme ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  static final light = ThemeData(
    useMaterial3: true,
    colorScheme: ColorScheme.fromSeed(
      seedColor: AppColors.primary,
      brightness: Brightness.light,
      surface: AppColors.lightSurface,
    ),
    scaffoldBackgroundColor: AppColors.lightBg,
    textTheme: _textTheme,
    elevatedButtonTheme: _elevatedButton,
    inputDecorationTheme: _inputTheme(AppColors.lightSurfaceLo),
    appBarTheme: const AppBarTheme(
      backgroundColor: AppColors.lightSurface,
      foregroundColor: AppColors.lightFg1,
      elevation: 0,
      scrolledUnderElevation: 1,
      centerTitle: false,
      titleTextStyle: TextStyle(
        color: AppColors.lightFg1,
        fontSize: 20,
        fontWeight: FontWeight.bold,
      ),
    ),
    cardTheme: CardTheme(
      color: AppColors.lightSurface,
      elevation: 0,
      margin: EdgeInsets.zero,
      shape: RoundedRectangleBorder(borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(16)),
    ),
    dividerColor: AppColors.lightHairline,
    iconTheme: const IconThemeData(color: AppColors.lightFg2),
  );

  // ── Dark theme ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  static final dark = ThemeData(
    useMaterial3: true,
    colorScheme: ColorScheme.fromSeed(
      seedColor: AppColors.primary,
      brightness: Brightness.dark,
      surface: AppColors.darkSurface,
    ),
    scaffoldBackgroundColor: AppColors.darkBg,
    textTheme: _textTheme,
    elevatedButtonTheme: _elevatedButton,
    inputDecorationTheme: _inputTheme(AppColors.darkSurfaceLo),
    appBarTheme: const AppBarTheme(
      backgroundColor: AppColors.darkSurface,
      foregroundColor: AppColors.darkFg1,
      elevation: 0,
      scrolledUnderElevation: 1,
      centerTitle: false,
      titleTextStyle: TextStyle(

    ),
    dividerColor: AppColors.darkHairline,
    iconTheme: const IconThemeData(color: AppColors.darkFg2),
  );
}
