import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'app_colors.dart';

abstract final class AppTheme {
  // ── Typography (generous sizes for older family members) ──────────────────
  static const _textTheme = TextTheme(
    bodySmall:      TextStyle(fontSize: 13),
    bodyMedium:     TextStyle(fontSize: 15),
    bodyLarge:      TextStyle(fontSize: 17),
    titleSmall:     TextStyle(fontSize: 15, fontWeight: FontWeight.w600),
    titleMedium:    TextStyle(fontSize: 17, fontWeight: FontWeight.w600),
    titleLarge:     TextStyle(fontSize: 20, fontWeight: FontWeight.bold),
    headlineSmall:  TextStyle(fontSize: 22, fontWeight: FontWeight.bold),
    headlineMedium: TextStyle(fontSize: 26, fontWeight: FontWeight.bold),
    headlineLarge:  TextStyle(fontSize: 32, fontWeight: FontWeight.w600),
  );

  // ── Shared input decoration (18 px radius, floating label) ────────────────
  static InputDecorationTheme _inputTheme(Color fill) => InputDecorationTheme(
        filled: true,
        fillColor: fill,
        floatingLabelBehavior: FloatingLabelBehavior.auto,
        contentPadding:
            const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 20, vertical: 20),
        border: OutlineInputBorder(
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(18),
          borderSide: BorderSide.none,
        ),
        enabledBorder: OutlineInputBorder(
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(18),
          borderSide: BorderSide.none,
        ),
        focusedBorder: OutlineInputBorder(
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(18),
          borderSide:
              const BorderSide(color: AppColors.primary, width: 2),
        ),
        errorBorder: OutlineInputBorder(
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(18),
          borderSide:
              const BorderSide(color: AppColors.danger, width: 1.5),
        ),
        focusedErrorBorder: OutlineInputBorder(
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(18),
          borderSide:
              const BorderSide(color: AppColors.danger, width: 2),
        ),
        labelStyle: const TextStyle(fontSize: 15),
        errorStyle: const TextStyle(color: AppColors.danger, fontSize: 12),
      );

  // ── Pill button (56 px tall, stadium shape) ───────────────────────────────
  static final _elevatedButton = ElevatedButtonThemeData(
    style: ElevatedButton.styleFrom(
      minimumSize: const Size(double.infinity, 56),
      shape: const StadiumBorder(),
      backgroundColor: AppColors.primary,
      foregroundColor: Colors.white,
      disabledBackgroundColor: AppColors.primary.withAlpha(100),
      textStyle: const TextStyle(
        fontSize: 17,
        fontWeight: FontWeight.w600,
        letterSpacing: 0.3,
      ),
      elevation: 0,
    ),
  );

  // ── Light theme ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  static final light = ThemeData(
    useMaterial3: true,
    colorScheme: ColorScheme.fromSeed(
      seedColor: AppColors.primary,
      brightness: Brightness.light,
      surface: AppColors.lightSurface,
    ),
    scaffoldBackgroundColor: AppColors.lightBg,
    textTheme: _textTheme,
    elevatedButtonTheme: _elevatedButton,
    inputDecorationTheme: _inputTheme(AppColors.lightSurfaceLo),
    appBarTheme: const AppBarTheme(
      backgroundColor: AppColors.lightSurface,
      foregroundColor: AppColors.lightFg1,
      elevation: 0,
      scrolledUnderElevation: 1,
      centerTitle: false,
      titleTextStyle: TextStyle(
        color: AppColors.lightFg1,
        fontSize: 20,
        fontWeight: FontWeight.bold,
      ),
    ),
    cardTheme: CardTheme(
      color: AppColors.lightSurface,
      elevation: 0,
      margin: EdgeInsets.zero,
      shape: RoundedRectangleBorder(borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(16)),
    ),
    dividerColor: AppColors.lightHairline,
    iconTheme: const IconThemeData(color: AppColors.lightFg2),
  );

  // ── Dark theme ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  static final dark = ThemeData(
    useMaterial3: true,
    colorScheme: ColorScheme.fromSeed(
      seedColor: AppColors.primary,
      brightness: Brightness.dark,
      surface: AppColors.darkSurface,
    ),
    scaffoldBackgroundColor: AppColors.darkBg,
    textTheme: _textTheme,
    elevatedButtonTheme: _elevatedButton,
    inputDecorationTheme: _inputTheme(AppColors.darkSurfaceLo),
    appBarTheme: const AppBarTheme(

`--split-per-abi` produces three small APKs (arm64, arm, x86_64) instead of one fat APK — faster and about 60 % smaller each.

**If you hit the file-lock error again** (e.g. after an interrupted build), run these three commands in your own terminal before rebuilding:

```powershell
# 1 — kill lingering Java/Gradle processes
taskkill /F /IM java.exe /T

# 2 — delete the locked directory
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "build\app\intermediates\stripped_native_libs" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

# 3 — full clean then rebuild
flutter clean
flutter build apk --split-per-abi
```

**Root cause of the lock:** Gradle spawns a background strip-symbols worker that writes `.temp-stream-*` files. If the build is interrupted (Ctrl-C, timeout, antivirus scan at the wrong moment), those worker processes stay alive with the file handles open. Killing `java.exe` + deleting the intermediate directory resets it completely.

content.text:
Now here's the full picture:

---

## How Flutter config works in this project

**Short answer: no `.env` for Flutter.** Flutter bakes config into the binary at compile time — it can't read files at runtime. The mechanism is `--dart-define-from-file`.

### The two config files just created

| File | When to use |
|---|---|
| `dart_defines/local.json` | Running on Android emulator (10.0.2.2 = your PC's localhost) |
| `dart_defines/production.json` | Building release APK against the live server |

**Before your first production build**, edit `production.json` to replace the placeholder domain:
```json
{
  "API_BASE_URL": "https://your-real-domain.com",
  "SIGNALING_URL": "wss://your-real-domain.com",
  "APP_ENV": "prod"
}
```

### Build commands

```powershell
# Development (emulator) — debug build
flutter run --dart-define-from-file=dart_defines/local.json

# Release APK for testing — still uses local backend
flutter build apk --split-per-abi --dart-define-from-file=dart_defines/local.json

# Production APK — uses your live server
flutter build apk --split-per-abi --dart-define-from-file=dart_defines/production.json
```

### How it flows

```
dart_defines/production.json
        ↓  --dart-define-from-file
  AppConfig.apiBaseUrl  (compile-time String.fromEnvironment)
        ↓  read by
  dio_client.dart → all API calls
  auth_repository.dart → auth calls
```

The backend `.env` (`familylink/.env`) is completely separate — it's only read by Docker Compose to configure Postgres, Redis, JWT signing keys, etc.

content.text:
Review target: `--effort max`

`high effort → 3 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 angles, up to 6 each)

Run **3 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`.

+"""
+Aggregate health checks for /health (JSON probes and HTML dashboard).
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import re
+import time
+import uuid
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from enum import Enum
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+from urllib.parse import urlparse
+
+import httpx
+import redis.asyncio as aioredis
+from sqlalchemy import text
+from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncEngine
+
+from app.config import settings
+from app.utils.storage import ensure_media_dirs
+
+_SIGNALING_HEALTH_URL = "http://signaling:8001/health"
+_NGINX_INTERNAL_HEALTH = "http://nginx/health?format=json"
+_PLACEHOLDER_RE = re.compile(r"REPLACE_WITH|CHANGE_ME|your-", re.I)
+_IPV4_RE = re.compile(
+    r"^(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|[01]?\d\d?)\.){3}"
+    r"(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|[01]?\d\d?)$"
+)
+
+
+class CheckStatus(str, Enum):
+    OK = "ok"
+    WARN = "warn"
+    ERROR = "error"
+
+
+class OverallStatus(str, Enum):
+    OK = "ok"
+    DEGRADED = "degraded"
+    DOWN = "down"
+
+
+@dataclass
+class HealthCheck:
+    name: str
+    status: CheckStatus
+    message: str
+    latency_ms: float | None = None
+    critical: bool = True
+
+    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        return {
+            "name": self.name,
+            "status": self.status.value,
+            "message": self.message,
+            "latency_ms": self.latency_ms,
+            "critical": self.critical,
+        }
+
+
+@dataclass
+class HealthReport:
+    status: OverallStatus
+    checks: list[HealthCheck] = field(default_factory=list)
+    attention: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    environment: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    generated_at: str = ""
+
+    @property
+    def http_status(self) -> int:
+        return 503 if self.status == OverallStatus.DOWN else 200
+
+    def to_json(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        return {
+            "status": self.status.value,
+            "checks": [c.to_dict() for c in self.checks],
+            "attention": self.attention,
+            "environment": self.environment,
+            "generated_at": self.generated_at,
+        }
+
+
+def wants_json_response(accept: str | None, format_param: str | None) -> bool:
+    """Whether a detailed /health response should be JSON (vs HTML dashboard)."""
+    if format_param == "html":
+        return False
+    if format_param in ("json", "full", "detailed"):
+        return True
+    if not accept:
+        return True
+    lowered = accept.lower()
+    if "text/html" in lowered and "application/json" not in lowered:
+        return False
+    if "application/json" in lowered:
+        return True
+    return True
+
+
+def wants_detailed_report(accept: str | None, format_param: str | None, detailed: bool) -> bool:
+    """
+    Full health dashboard / JSON report — expensive (DB, Redis, HTTP, TCP probes).
+
+    Lightweight {"status":"ok"} is used for probes, bots, and deploy scripts.
+    """
+    if detailed:
+        return True
+    if format_param in ("full", "detailed"):
+        return True
+    if format_param == "html":
+        return True
+    if not accept:
+        return False

+    "build",

+        return True
+    return any(p in SKIP_DIRS for p in parts)
+
+
+def upload_tree(sftp: paramiko.SFTPClient, local_root: Path, remote_root: str) -> None:
+    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(local_root):
+        rel_root = Path(root).relative_to(local_root)
+        if should_skip(rel_root):
+            dirs[:] = []
+            continue
+        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in SKIP_DIRS]
+        remote_dir = remote_root if rel_root == Path(".") else f"{remote_root}/{rel_root.as_posix()}"

+            sftp.mkdir(remote_dir)
+        for name in files:
+            if name in SKIP_FILES:

+            rel = rel_root / name
+            if should_skip(rel.parent):
+                continue
+            local_path = Path(root) / name
+            remote_path = f"{remote_dir}/{name}"
+            sftp.put(str(local_path), remote_path)
+
+
+def run(ssh: paramiko.SSHClient, cmd: str, timeout: int = 1800) -> None:
+    print(f"\n>>> {cmd}")
+    _, stdout, stderr = ssh.exec_command(cmd, timeout=timeout)
+    out = stdout.read().decode()
+    err = stderr.read().decode()
+    code = stdout.channel.recv_exit_status()
+    if out:
+        sys.stdout.buffer.write(out.encode("utf-8", "replace"))
+        if not out.endswith("\n"):

+    if err:

+    if code != 0:

+

+    local_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

All three angles complete. Here's the full ranked report:

---

## Cursor Branch Review — 10 Findings

### 🔴 Critical (fix before any real user traffic)

**1. TURN secret + server IP hardcoded in git — `deploy/finish_deploy.py` lines 7–9**
```python
HOST = "[REDACTED_VPS_IP]"                          # real server IP committed
TURN_SECRET = "REDACTED_TURN_SECRET"  # ← leaked
```
Anyone with repo read access can forge valid TURN credentials and use your Coturn server as a free relay. The secret should be `os.environ["TURN_SECRET"]` and rotated immediately. The IP should move to an env var too.

---

**2. `uiOnly` defaults to `true` in production — `flutter_app/lib/core/config/app_config.dart` line 39**
```dart
static const bool uiOnly = bool.hasEnvironment('UI_ONLY')
    ? bool.fromEnvironment('UI_ONLY')
    : true;   // ← production APK ships with mock data unless explicitly disabled
```
Running `flutter build apk` without `--dart-define=UI_ONLY=false` produces an APK that skips all real auth and shows "Rose Martinez" as the user identity. The safe default should be `false`:
```dart
: false;   // default OFF — enable only for UI-preview builds
```

---

### 🟠 High (correctness bugs)

**3. `calls_router` mounted under `/api/auth` instead of `/api/calls` — `backend/api/app/main.py` line ~127**
```python
app.include_router(calls_router.router, prefix="/api/auth", tags=["calls"])  # wrong
```
The TURN credentials endpoint ends up at `GET /api/auth/turn-credentials` — the Flutter client will call `/api/calls/turn-credentials` and get a 404. Every WebRTC call will fail to get ICE credentials. Fix: `prefix="/api/calls"`.

---

**4. Health endpoint leaks DB error strings unauthenticated — `backend/api/app/services/health_service.py` lines ~148, ~170**

When Postgres or Redis is unreachable, `message=str(exc)` is returned verbatim in the public `/health?detailed=true` JSON. SQLAlchemy exceptions routinely include the full `DATABASE_URL` with the password. Fix: sanitize exception messages:
```python
message=f"Connection failed: {type(exc).__name__}"
```

---

**5. `/health?detailed=true` exposes internal topology unauthenticated — `health_service.py` ~line 398**

`_build_environment()` embeds `postgres_db`, `redis_host`, `turn_host`, `domain`, and `debug` status into the public unauthenticated response. Add a `Bearer` token check (or restrict to the Docker internal network only) before serving the detailed report.

---

### 🟡 Medium (functional gaps / integration issues)

**6. `MediaViewer` has no `url` parameter — `flutter_app/lib/app.dart` line ~110**

The route passes `kind/sender/when` but `MediaViewer` only renders `CustomPaint` mock artwork. When the real backend is wired, navigating to `/media` will silently show mock art instead of the real image/video. Also: any `kind` value outside `image/video/document` (e.g. `audio`) silently falls through to the document viewer.

---

**7. `ChatRichScreen` shows wrong mock data for real conversation IDs — `chat_rich_screen.dart` line ~83**

Any `conversationId` that isn't literally `'rose'`, `'mike'`, or `'fam'` silently displays "Family Member" and a generic message thread with no loading/error state. When real backend UUIDs are passed, users see stale mock data with no indication anything is wrong.

---

**8. `.env` not excluded from `remote_deploy.py` upload — `deploy/remote_deploy.py`**

`SKIP_FILES` excludes `firebase-service-account.json` and `google-services.json` but not `.env`. The intent is to upload `.env` to the server (correct), but there's no guardrail preventing `git add .env`. Add `.env` to the repo's root `.gitignore` (it's already in `.gitignore` for the backend dir) and add an assertion in the deploy script that `.env` is not git-tracked before uploading.

---

### ⚪ Low / Maintenance

**9. Dead code in `auth_notifier._tryRestoreSession` — `auth_notifier.dart` line 34**

The `if (AppConfig.uiOnly) { … return; }` guard inside `_tryRestoreSession` is unreachable — the constructor's `else` branch already prevents calling the method when `uiOnly` is true. Safe to delete; it's a maintenance trap if the constructor is ever refactored.

---

**10. `file_picker` pinned to exact version — `pubspec.yaml` line 42**

`file_picker: 11.0.2` (no `^`) deviates from every other dependency. If this version is retracted from pub.dev or conflicts with a transitive constraint, `pub get` fails with no fallback. Change to `file_picker: ^11.0.2`.

---

## Overall Assessment

| Area | Status |

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import sys

import paramiko

HOST = "[REDACTED_VPS_IP]"
PASSWORD = os.environ["DEPLOY_PASSWORD"]
TURN_SECRET = "REDACTED_TURN_SECRET"
REMOTE = "/opt/lumin"


def run(ssh, cmd, timeout=600):
    print(f">>> {cmd}")
    _, stdout, stderr = ssh.exec_command(cmd, timeout=timeout)
    out = stdout.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    err = stderr.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    code = stdout.channel.recv_exit_status()
    if out:
        print(out)
    if err:
        print(err, file=sys.stderr)
    if code != 0:
        raise SystemExit(code)


def main():
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    ssh = paramiko.SSHClient()
    ssh.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.AutoAddPolicy())
    ssh.connect(HOST, username="root", password=PASSWORD, timeout=60)

    run(ssh, "apt-get install -y -qq dos2unix")
    run(ssh, f'find {REMOTE} -name "*.sh" -exec dos2unix {{}} +')
    run(
        ssh,
        f"cd {REMOTE} && docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml "
        "exec -T fastapi alembic stamp head",
    )
    run(
        ssh,
        f"cd {REMOTE} && VPS_PUBLIC_IP={HOST} DOMAIN={HOST} "
        f"TURN_SECRET={TURN_SECRET} bash coturn/install.sh",
    )
    run(ssh, f"cd {REMOTE} && bash coturn/firewall.sh --yes", timeout=120)
    run(ssh, f"curl -fsS http://{HOST}/health")
    run(ssh, "systemctl is-active coturn")
    ssh.close()
    print("Post-deploy steps complete.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
Lumin FastAPI application factory.
"""
import logging
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from pathlib import Path

import redis.asyncio as aioredis
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query, Request
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates
from sqlalchemy import text

from app.config import settings
from app.db import engine
from app.services.health_service import (
    collect_health,
    wants_detailed_report,
    wants_json_response,
)
from app.routers import auth as auth_router
from app.routers import calls as calls_router
from app.routers import contacts as contacts_router
from app.routers import conversations as conversations_router
from app.routers import media as media_router
from app.routers import messages as messages_router
from app.routers import users as users_router
from app.utils.exceptions import AppError
from app.utils.storage import ensure_media_dirs

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

templates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "templates"))


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncGenerator[None, None]:
    # ── Startup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    redis_client = aioredis.from_url(
        settings.REDIS_URL,
        encoding="utf-8",
        decode_responses=True,
    )
    await redis_client.ping()
    app.state.redis = redis_client
    logger.info("Redis connected at %s", settings.REDIS_URL)

    async with engine.connect() as conn:
        await conn.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
    logger.info("Database connection verified")

    ensure_media_dirs()
    logger.info("Media directories verified at %s", settings.MEDIA_BASE_PATH)

    yield

    # ── Shutdown ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    await redis_client.aclose()
    await engine.dispose()
    logger.info("Connections closed")


def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    app = FastAPI(
        title="Lumin API",
        version="1.0.0",
        lifespan=lifespan,
        # Disable interactive docs in production
        docs_url="/api/docs" if settings.DEBUG else None,
        redoc_url=None,
    )

    # ── CORS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # The client is a mobile app — there is no browser origin restriction needed.
    # Auth is header-based (Bearer token), not cookies, so wildcard is safe here.
    app.add_middleware(
        CORSMiddleware,
        allow_origins=["*"],
        allow_methods=["*"],
        allow_headers=["*"],
    )

    # ── Exception handlers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @app.exception_handler(AppError)
    async def _app_error(request: Request, exc: AppError) -> JSONResponse:
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=exc.status_code,
            content={"detail": exc.detail, "code": exc.code},
        )

    @app.exception_handler(Exception)
    async def _unhandled(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
        logger.exception("Unhandled error on %s %s", request.method, request.url)
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=500,
            content={"detail": "Internal server error", "code": "internal_error"},
        )

    # ── Routes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @app.get("/health", tags=["infra"])
    async def health(
        request: Request,
        format: str | None = Query(default=None, alias="format"),
        detailed: bool = Query(default=False, alias="detailed"),
    ):
        accept = request.headers.get("accept")
        if not wants_detailed_report(accept, format, detailed):
            return JSONResponse(content={"status": "ok"})
        report = await collect_health(request.app.state.redis, engine)
        if wants_json_response(accept, format):
            return JSONResponse(
                content=report.to_json(),
                status_code=report.http_status,
            )
        return templates.TemplateResponse(
            request=request,
            name="health.html",
            context={"report": report},
            status_code=report.http_status,
        )

    app.include_router(auth_router.router, prefix="/api/auth", tags=["auth"])
    app.include_router(calls_router.router, prefix="/api/auth", tags=["calls"])
    app.include_router(users_router.router, prefix="/api/users", tags=["users"])
    app.include_router(contacts_router.router, prefix="/api/contacts", tags=["contacts"])
    app.include_router(conversations_router.router, prefix="/api/conversations", tags=["conversations"])
    app.include_router(messages_router.router, prefix="/api/messages", tags=["messages"])
    app.include_router(media_router.router, prefix="/api/media", tags=["media"])

    return app


app = create_app()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Upload Lumin stack to VPS and start Docker Compose (excludes flutter_app)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import stat
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import paramiko

HOST = os.environ.get("DEPLOY_HOST", "[REDACTED_VPS_IP]")
USER = os.environ.get("DEPLOY_USER", "root")
PASSWORD = os.environ["DEPLOY_PASSWORD"]
REMOTE_DIR = os.environ.get("DEPLOY_DIR", "/opt/lumin")

SKIP_DIRS = {
    ".git",
    "flutter_app",
    "node_modules",
    "__pycache__",
    ".pytest_cache",
    ".dart_tool",
    "build",
    "docs",
    ".cursor",
    "agent-transcripts",
    "terminals",
    "mcps",
}
SKIP_FILES = {".DS_Store", "firebase-service-account.json", "google-services.json"}


def should_skip(rel: Path) -> bool:
    parts = rel.parts
    if parts and parts[0] in SKIP_DIRS:
        return True
    return any(p in SKIP_DIRS for p in parts)


def upload_tree(sftp: paramiko.SFTPClient, local_root: Path, remote_root: str) -> None:
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(local_root):
        rel_root = Path(root).relative_to(local_root)
        if should_skip(rel_root):
            dirs[:] = []
            continue
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in SKIP_DIRS]
        remote_dir = remote_root if rel_root == Path(".") else f"{remote_root}/{rel_root.as_posix()}"
        try:
            sftp.stat(remote_dir)
        except OSError:
            sftp.mkdir(remote_dir)
        for name in files:
            if name in SKIP_FILES:
                continue
            rel = rel_root / name
            if should_skip(rel.parent):
                continue
            local_path = Path(root) / name
            remote_path = f"{remote_dir}/{name}"
            sftp.put(str(local_path), remote_path)


def run(ssh: paramiko.SSHClient, cmd: str, timeout: int = 1800) -> None:
    print(f"\n>>> {cmd}")
    _, stdout, stderr = ssh.exec_command(cmd, timeout=timeout)
    out = stdout.read().decode()
    err = stderr.read().decode()
    code = stdout.channel.recv_exit_status()
    if out:
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(out.encode("utf-8", "replace"))
        if not out.endswith("\n"):
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(b"\n")
    if err:
        sys.stderr.buffer.write(err.encode("utf-8", "replace"))
        if not err.endswith("\n"):
            sys.stderr.buffer.write(b"\n")
    if code != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Command failed ({code}): {cmd}")


def main() -> None:
    local_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    ssh = paramiko.SSHClient()
    ssh.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.AutoAddPolicy())
    print(f"Connecting to {USER}@{HOST}...")
    ssh.connect(HOST, username=USER, password=PASSWORD, timeout=60)

    run(
        ssh,
        "export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive; "
        "command -v docker >/dev/null || curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh; "
        "systemctl enable --now docker; "
        "docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1 || apt-get update -qq && "
        "apt-get install -y -qq docker-compose-plugin; "
        "mkdir -p /var/app-media /var/www/certbot " + REMOTE_DIR,
        timeout=600,
    )

    print("Uploading project files...")
    sftp = ssh.open_sftp()
    try:
        try:
            sftp.stat(REMOTE_DIR)
        except OSError:
            sftp.mkdir(REMOTE_DIR)
        upload_tree(sftp, local_root, REMOTE_DIR)
    finally:
        sftp.close()

    turn_secret = None
    env_path = local_root / ".env"
    for line in env_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("TURN_SECRET="):
            turn_secret = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
            break

    compose = (
        f"cd {REMOTE_DIR} && "
        "docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml "
        "up -d --build"
    )
    run(ssh, compose, timeout=1800)

    run(ssh, "apt-get install -y -qq dos2unix && find " + REMOTE_DIR + ' -name "*.sh" -exec dos2unix {} +', timeout=120)
    run(
        ssh,
        f"cd {REMOTE_DIR} && docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml "
        "exec -T fastapi alembic stamp head",
        timeout=300,
    )

    if turn_secret:
        run(
            ssh,
            f"cd {REMOTE_DIR} && "
            f"export VPS_PUBLIC_IP={HOST} DOMAIN={HOST} TURN_SECRET='{turn_secret}' && "
            "bash coturn/install.sh",
            timeout=300,
        )
        run(ssh, f"cd {REMOTE_DIR} && bash coturn/firewall.sh --yes", timeout=120)

    run(ssh, f"curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1/health || curl -fsS http://localhost/health", timeout=30)
    print(f"\nDeploy complete. API: http://{HOST}/api/docs (if DEBUG)  Health: http://{HOST}/health")
    ssh.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "DEPLOY_PASSWORD" not in os.environ:
        print("Set DEPLOY_PASSWORD", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import sys

import paramiko

HOST = "[REDACTED_VPS_IP]"
PASSWORD = os.environ["DEPLOY_PASSWORD"]
TURN_SECRET = "REDACTED_TURN_SECRET"
REMOTE = "/opt/lumin"


def run(ssh, cmd, timeout=600):
    print(f">>> {cmd}")
    _, stdout, stderr = ssh.exec_command(cmd, timeout=timeout)
    out = stdout.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    err = stderr.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    code = stdout.channel.recv_exit_status()
    if out:
        print(out)
    if err:
        print(err, file=sys.stderr)
    if code != 0:
        raise SystemExit(code)


def main():
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    ssh = paramiko.SSHClient()
    ssh.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.AutoAddPolicy())
    ssh.connect(HOST, username="root", password=PASSWORD, timeout=60)

    run(ssh, "apt-get install -y -qq dos2unix")
    run(ssh, f'find {REMOTE} -name "*.sh" -exec dos2unix {{}} +')
    run(
        ssh,
        f"cd {REMOTE} && docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml "
        "exec -T fastapi alembic stamp head",
    )
    run(
        ssh,
        f"cd {REMOTE} && VPS_PUBLIC_IP={HOST} DOMAIN={HOST} "
        f"TURN_SECRET={TURN_SECRET} bash coturn/install.sh",
    )
    run(ssh, f"cd {REMOTE} && bash coturn/firewall.sh --yes", timeout=120)
    run(ssh, f"curl -fsS http://{HOST}/health")
    run(ssh, "systemctl is-active coturn")
    ssh.close()
    print("Post-deploy steps complete.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
Lumin FastAPI application factory.
"""
import logging
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from pathlib import Path

import redis.asyncio as aioredis
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query, Request
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates
from sqlalchemy import text

from app.config import settings
from app.db import engine
from app.services.health_service import (
    collect_health,
    wants_detailed_report,
    wants_json_response,
)
from app.routers import auth as auth_router
from app.routers import calls as calls_router
from app.routers import contacts as contacts_router
from app.routers import conversations as conversations_router
from app.routers import media as media_router
from app.routers import messages as messages_router
from app.routers import users as users_router
from app.utils.exceptions import AppError
from app.utils.storage import ensure_media_dirs

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

templates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "templates"))


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncGenerator[None, None]:
    # ── Startup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    redis_client = aioredis.from_url(
        settings.REDIS_URL,
        encoding="utf-8",
        decode_responses=True,
    )
    await redis_client.ping()
    app.state.redis = redis_client
    logger.info("Redis connected at %s", settings.REDIS_URL)

    async with engine.connect() as conn:
        await conn.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
    logger.info("Database connection verified")

    ensure_media_dirs()
    logger.info("Media directories verified at %s", settings.MEDIA_BASE_PATH)

    yield

    # ── Shutdown ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    await redis_client.aclose()
    await engine.dispose()
    logger.info("Connections closed")


def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    app = FastAPI(
        title="Lumin API",
        version="1.0.0",
        lifespan=lifespan,
        # Disable interactive docs in production
        docs_url="/api/docs" if settings.DEBUG else None,
        redoc_url=None,
    )

    # ── CORS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # The client is a mobile app — there is no browser origin restriction needed.
    # Auth is header-based (Bearer token), not cookies, so wildcard is safe here.
    app.add_middleware(
        CORSMiddleware,
        allow_origins=["*"],
        allow_methods=["*"],
        allow_headers=["*"],
    )

    # ── Exception handlers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @app.exception_handler(AppError)
    async def _app_error(request: Request, exc: AppError) -> JSONResponse:
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=exc.status_code,
            content={"detail": exc.detail, "code": exc.code},
        )

    @app.exception_handler(Exception)
    async def _unhandled(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
        logger.exception("Unhandled error on %s %s", request.method, request.url)
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=500,
            content={"detail": "Internal server error", "code": "internal_error"},
        )

    # ── Routes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @app.get("/health", tags=["infra"])
    async def health(
        request: Request,
        format: str | None = Query(default=None, alias="format"),
        detailed: bool = Query(default=False, alias="detailed"),
    ):
        accept = request.headers.get("accept")
        if not wants_detailed_report(accept, format, detailed):
            return JSONResponse(content={"status": "ok"})
        report = await collect_health(request.app.state.redis, engine)
        if wants_json_response(accept, format):
            return JSONResponse(
                content=report.to_json(),
                status_code=report.http_status,
            )
        return templates.TemplateResponse(
            request=request,
            name="health.html",
            context={"report": report},
            status_code=report.http_status,
        )

    app.include_router(auth_router.router, prefix="/api/auth", tags=["auth"])
    app.include_router(calls_router.router, prefix="/api/auth", tags=["calls"])
    app.include_router(users_router.router, prefix="/api/users", tags=["users"])
    app.include_router(contacts_router.router, prefix="/api/contacts", tags=["contacts"])
    app.include_router(conversations_router.router, prefix="/api/conversations", tags=["conversations"])
    app.include_router(messages_router.router, prefix="/api/messages", tags=["messages"])
    app.include_router(media_router.router, prefix="/api/media", tags=["media"])

    return app


app = create_app()

SKIP_DIRS = {
    ".git",
    "flutter_app",
    "node_modules",
    "__pycache__",
    ".pytest_cache",
    ".dart_tool",
    "build",
    "docs",
    ".cursor",
    "agent-transcripts",
    "terminals",
    "mcps",
}
SKIP_FILES = {".DS_Store", "firebase-service-account.json", "google-services.json"}


def should_skip(rel: Path) -> bool:
    parts = rel.parts
    if parts and parts[0] in SKIP_DIRS:
        return True
    return any(p in SKIP_DIRS for p in parts)


def upload_tree(sftp: paramiko.SFTPClient, local_root: Path, remote_root: str) -> None:
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(local_root):
        rel_root = Path(root).relative_to(local_root)
        if should_skip(rel_root):
            dirs[:] = []
            continue
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in SKIP_DIRS]
        remote_dir = remote_root if rel_root == Path(".") else f"{remote_root}/{rel_root.as_posix()}"
        try:
            sftp.stat(remote_dir)
        except OSError:
            sftp.mkdir(remote_dir)
        for name in files:
            if name in SKIP_FILES:
                continue
            rel = rel_root / name
            if should_skip(rel.parent):
                continue
            local_path = Path(root) / name
            remote_path = f"{remote_dir}/{name}"
            sftp.put(str(local_path), remote_path)


def run(ssh: paramiko.SSHClient, cmd: str, timeout: int = 1800) -> None:
    print(f"\n>>> {cmd}")
    _, stdout, stderr = ssh.exec_command(cmd, timeout=timeout)
    out = stdout.read().decode()
    err = stderr.read().decode()
    code = stdout.channel.recv_exit_status()
    if out:
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(out.encode("utf-8", "replace"))
        if not out.endswith("\n"):
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(b"\n")
    if err:
        sys.stderr.buffer.write(err.encode("utf-8", "replace"))
        if not err.endswith("\n"):
            sys.stderr.buffer.write(b"\n")
    if code != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Command failed ({code}): {cmd}")


def main() -> None:
    local_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    ssh = paramiko.SSHClient()
    ssh.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.AutoAddPolicy())
    print(f"Connecting to {USER}@{HOST}...")
    ssh.connect(HOST, username=USER, password=PASSWORD, timeout=60)

    run(
        ssh,
        "export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive; "
        "command -v docker >/dev/null || curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh; "
        "systemctl enable --now docker; "
        "docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1 || apt-get update -qq && "
        "apt-get install -y -qq docker-compose-plugin; "
        "mkdir -p /var/app-media /var/www/certbot " + REMOTE_DIR,
        timeout=600,
    )

    print("Uploading project files...")
    sftp = ssh.open_sftp()
    try:
        try:
            sftp.stat(REMOTE_DIR)
        except OSError:
            sftp.mkdir(REMOTE_DIR)
        upload_tree(sftp, local_root, REMOTE_DIR)
    finally:
        sftp.close()

    turn_secret = None
    env_path = local_root / ".env"
    for line in env_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("TURN_SECRET="):
            turn_secret = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
            break

    compose = (
        f"cd {REMOTE_DIR} && "
        "docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml "
        "up -d --build"
    )
    run(ssh, compose, timeout=1800)

    run(ssh, "apt-get install -y -qq dos2unix && find " + REMOTE_DIR + ' -name "*.sh" -exec dos2unix {} +', timeout=120)
    run(
        ssh,
        f"cd {REMOTE_DIR} && docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml "
        "exec -T fastapi alembic stamp head",
        timeout=300,
    )

    if turn_secret:
        run(
            ssh,
            f"cd {REMOTE_DIR} && "
            f"export VPS_PUBLIC_IP={HOST} DOMAIN={HOST} TURN_SECRET='{turn_secret}' && "
            "bash coturn/install.sh",
            timeout=300,
        )
        run(ssh, f"cd {REMOTE_DIR} && bash coturn/firewall.sh --yes", timeout=120)

    run(ssh, f"curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1/health || curl -fsS http://localhost/health", timeout=30)
    print(f"\nDeploy complete. API: http://{HOST}/api/docs (if DEBUG)  Health: http://{HOST}/health")
    ssh.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "DEPLOY_PASSWORD" not in os.environ:
        print("Set DEPLOY_PASSWORD", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Upload Lumin stack to VPS and start Docker Compose (excludes flutter_app)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import stat
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import paramiko

HOST = os.environ.get("DEPLOY_HOST", "[REDACTED_VPS_IP]")
USER = os.environ.get("DEPLOY_USER", "root")
PASSWORD = os.environ["DEPLOY_PASSWORD"]
REMOTE_DIR = os.environ.get("DEPLOY_DIR", "/opt/lumin")

SKIP_DIRS = {
    ".git",
    "flutter_app",
    "node_modules",
    "__pycache__",
    ".pytest_cache",
    ".dart_tool",
    "build",
    "docs",
    ".cursor",
    "agent-transcripts",
    "terminals",
    "mcps",
}
SKIP_FILES = {".DS_Store", "firebase-service-account.json", "google-services.json"}


def should_skip(rel: Path) -> bool:
    parts = rel.parts
    if parts and parts[0] in SKIP_DIRS:
        return True
    return any(p in SKIP_DIRS for p in parts)


def upload_tree(sftp: paramiko.SFTPClient, local_root: Path, remote_root: str) -> None:
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(local_root):
        rel_root = Path(root).relative_to(local_root)
        if should_skip(rel_root):
            dirs[:] = []
            continue
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in SKIP_DIRS]
        remote_dir = remote_root if rel_root == Path(".") else f"{remote_root}/{rel_root.as_posix()}"
        try:
            sftp.stat(remote_dir)
        except OSError:
            sftp.mkdir(remote_dir)
        for name in files:
            if name in SKIP_FILES:
                continue
            rel = rel_root / name
            if should_skip(rel.parent):
                continue
            local_path = Path(root) / name
            remote_path = f"{remote_dir}/{name}"
            sftp.put(str(local_path), remote_path)


def run(ssh: paramiko.SSHClient, cmd: str, timeout: int = 1800) -> None:
    print(f"\n>>> {cmd}")
    _, stdout, stderr = ssh.exec_command(cmd, timeout=timeout)
    out = stdout.read().decode()
    err = stderr.read().decode()
    code = stdout.channel.recv_exit_status()
    if out:
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(out.encode("utf-8", "replace"))
        if not out.endswith("\n"):
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(b"\n")
    if err:
        sys.stderr.buffer.write(err.encode("utf-8", "replace"))
        if not err.endswith("\n"):
            sys.stderr.buffer.write(b"\n")
    if code != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Command failed ({code}): {cmd}")


def main() -> None:
    local_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    ssh = paramiko.SSHClient()
    ssh.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.AutoAddPolicy())
    print(f"Connecting to {USER}@{HOST}...")
    ssh.connect(HOST, username=USER, password=PASSWORD, timeout=60)

    run(
        ssh,
        "export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive; "
        "command -v docker >/dev/null || curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh; "
        "systemctl enable --now docker; "
        "docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1 || apt-get update -qq && "
        "apt-get install -y -qq docker-compose-plugin; "
        "mkdir -p /var/app-media /var/www/certbot " + REMOTE_DIR,
        timeout=600,
    )

    print("Uploading project files...")
    sftp = ssh.open_sftp()
    try:
        try:
            sftp.stat(REMOTE_DIR)
        except OSError:
            sftp.mkdir(REMOTE_DIR)
        upload_tree(sftp, local_root, REMOTE_DIR)
    finally:
        sftp.close()

    turn_secret = None
    env_path = local_root / ".env"
    for line in env_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("TURN_SECRET="):
            turn_secret = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
            break

    compose = (
        f"cd {REMOTE_DIR} && "
        "docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml "
        "up -d --build"
    )
    run(ssh, compose, timeout=1800)

    run(ssh, "apt-get install -y -qq dos2unix && find " + REMOTE_DIR + ' -name "*.sh" -exec dos2unix {} +', timeout=120)
    run(
        ssh,
        f"cd {REMOTE_DIR} && docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml "
        "exec -T fastapi alembic stamp head",
        timeout=300,
    )

    if turn_secret:
        run(
            ssh,
            f"cd {REMOTE_DIR} && "
            f"export VPS_PUBLIC_IP={HOST} DOMAIN={HOST} TURN_SECRET='{turn_secret}' && "
            "bash coturn/install.sh",
            timeout=300,
        )
        run(ssh, f"cd {REMOTE_DIR} && bash coturn/firewall.sh --yes", timeout=120)

    run(ssh, f"curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1/health || curl -fsS http://localhost/health", timeout=30)
    print(f"\nDeploy complete. API: http://{HOST}/api/docs (if DEBUG)  Health: http://{HOST}/health")
    ssh.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "DEPLOY_PASSWORD" not in os.environ:
        print("Set DEPLOY_PASSWORD", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Usage:
#   export DEPLOY_HOST=<vps-ip>
#   export DEPLOY_PASSWORD=<ssh-password>
#   export TURN_SECRET=<secret-from-dotenv>   # rotate the old one — it was leaked
#   python deploy/finish_deploy.py
import os
import sys

import paramiko

HOST = os.environ["DEPLOY_HOST"]          # never hard-code the server IP
PASSWORD = os.environ["DEPLOY_PASSWORD"]
TURN_SECRET = os.environ["TURN_SECRET"]   # never hard-code — was leaked, must rotate
REMOTE = "/opt/lumin"


def _validate_env() -> None:
    missing = [k for k in ("DEPLOY_HOST", "DEPLOY_PASSWORD", "TURN_SECRET") if not os.environ.get(k)]
    if missing:
        print(f"Missing required env vars: {', '.join(missing)}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


def run(ssh, cmd, timeout=600):
    print(f">>> {cmd}")
    _, stdout, stderr = ssh.exec_command(cmd, timeout=timeout)
    out = stdout.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    err = stderr.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    code = stdout.channel.recv_exit_status()
    if out:
        print(out)
    if err:
        print(err, file=sys.stderr)
    if code != 0:
        raise SystemExit(code)


def main():
    _validate_env()
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    ssh = paramiko.SSHClient()
    ssh.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.AutoAddPolicy())
    ssh.connect(HOST, username="root", password=PASSWORD, timeout=60)

    run(ssh, "apt-get install -y -qq dos2unix")
    run(ssh, f'find {REMOTE} -name "*.sh" -exec dos2unix {{}} +')
    run(
        ssh,
        f"cd {REMOTE} && docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml "
        "exec -T fastapi alembic stamp head",
    )
    run(
        ssh,
        f"cd {REMOTE} && VPS_PUBLIC_IP={HOST} DOMAIN={HOST} "
        f"TURN_SECRET={TURN_SECRET} bash coturn/install.sh",
    )
    run(ssh, f"cd {REMOTE} && bash coturn/firewall.sh --yes", timeout=120)
    run(ssh, f"curl -fsS http://{HOST}/health")
    run(ssh, "systemctl is-active coturn")
    ssh.close()
    print("Post-deploy steps complete.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# ── Routes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _is_internal(request: Request) -> bool:
        """
        Returns True only for requests that originate from localhost or a
        private RFC-1918 / Docker-internal address.

        Nginx sets X-Real-IP; fall back to the raw ASGI client IP.
        The detailed health report (topology + environment) must never be
        served to external callers unauthenticated.
        """
        ip = request.headers.get("x-real-ip") or (
            request.client.host if request.client else ""
        )
        return ip in ("127.0.0.1", "::1", "localhost") or ip.startswith(
            ("10.", "172.16.", "172.17.", "172.18.", "172.19.", "172.20.",
             "172.21.", "172.22.", "172.23.", "172.24.", "172.25.", "172.26.",
             "172.27.", "172.28.", "172.29.", "172.30.", "172.31.", "192.168.")
        )

    @app.get("/health", tags=["infra"])
    async def health(
        request: Request,
        format: str | None = Query(default=None, alias="format"),
        detailed: bool = Query(default=False, alias="detailed"),
    ):
        accept = request.headers.get("accept")
        # Detailed report exposes internal topology — restrict to internal callers.
        if not wants_detailed_report(accept, format, detailed) or not _is_internal(request):
            return JSONResponse(content={"status": "ok"})
        report = await collect_health(request.app.state.redis, engine)
        if wants_json_response(accept, format):
            return JSONResponse(
                content=report.to_json(),
                status_code=report.http_status,
            )
        return templates.TemplateResponse(
            request=request,
            name="health.html",
            context={"report": report},
            status_code=report.http_status,
        )

    app.include_router(auth_router.router, prefix="/api/auth", tags=["auth"])
    app.include_router(calls_router.router, prefix="/api/calls", tags=["calls"])
    app.include_router(users_router.router, prefix="/api/users", tags=["users"])
    app.include_router(contacts_router.router, prefix="/api/contacts", tags=["contacts"])
    app.include_router(conversations_router.router, prefix="/api/conversations", tags=["conversations"])
    app.include_router(messages_router.router, prefix="/api/messages", tags=["messages"])
    app.include_router(media_router.router, prefix="/api/media", tags=["media"])

    return app


app = create_app()

```
connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream, upstream: "http://172.18.0.4:8000/health"
```

Nginx is trying to connect to `172.18.0.4:8000` but getting connection refused. The issue is that Nginx has a **stale/cached IP** for the `fastapi` container. When the fastapi container was recreated (during the `up -d --build`), it got a new IP address, but Nginx is still using the old IP (`172.18.0.4`) from when it was started 2 days ago.


The fix is to reload Nginx so it re-resolves the `fastapi` hostname to the new IP address. I can either restart the Nginx container or send it a reload signal to pick up the updated DNS resolution. This is a classic Docker networking issue where long-running containers maintain stale DNS caches when other services are recreated with new IPs.

Large diff — 127 files. Let me run all three review angles in parallel plus read the critical security-sensitive files simultaneously.
All three angles complete. Here's the full ranked report:
---
## Cursor Branch Review — 10 Findings
### 🔴 Critical (fix before any real user traffic)
**1. TURN secret + server IP hardcoded in git — `deploy/finish_deploy.py` lines 7–9**
```python
HOST = "[REDACTED_VPS_IP]"                          # real server IP committed
TURN_SECRET = "REDACTED_TURN_SECRET"  # ← leaked
```
Anyone with repo read access can forge valid TURN credentials and use your Coturn server as a free relay. The secret should be `os.environ["TURN_SECRET"]` and rotated immediately. The IP should move to an env var too.
---
**2. `uiOnly` defaults to `true` in production — `flutter_app/lib/core/config/app_config.dart` line 39**
```dart
static const bool uiOnly = bool.hasEnvironment('UI_ONLY')
    ? bool.fromEnvironment('UI_ONLY')
    : true;   // ← production APK ships with mock data unless explicitly disabled
```
Running `flutter build apk` without `--dart-define=UI_ONLY=false` produces an APK that skips all real auth and shows "Rose Martinez" as the user identity. The safe default should be `false`:
```dart
: false;   // default OFF — enable only for UI-preview builds
```
---
### 🟠 High (correctness bugs)
**3. `calls_router` mounted under `/api/auth` instead of `/api/calls` — `backend/api/app/main.py` line ~127**
```python
app.include_router(calls_router.router, prefix="/api/auth", tags=["calls"])  # wrong
```
The TURN credentials endpoint ends up at `GET /api/auth/turn-credentials` — the Flutter client will call `/api/calls/turn-credentials` and get a 404. Every WebRTC call will fail to get ICE credentials. Fix: `prefix="/api/calls"`.
---
**4. Health endpoint leaks DB error strings unauthenticated — `backend/api/app/services/health_service.py` lines ~148, ~170**
When Postgres or Redis is unreachable, `message=str(exc)` is returned verbatim in the public `/health?detailed=true` JSON. SQLAlchemy exceptions routinely include the full `DATABASE_URL` with the password. Fix: sanitize exception messages:
```python
message=f"Connection failed: {type(exc).__name__}"
```
---
**5. `/health?detailed=true` exposes internal topology unauthenticated — `health_service.py` ~line 398**
`_build_environment()` embeds `postgres_db`, `redis_host`, `turn_host`, `domain`, and `debug` status into the public unauthenticated response. Add a `Bearer` token check (or restrict to the Docker internal network only) before serving the detailed report.
---
### 🟡 Medium (functional gaps / integration issues)
**6. `MediaViewer` has no `url` parameter — `flutter_app/lib/app.dart` line ~110**
The route passes `kind/sender/when` but `MediaViewer` only renders `CustomPaint` mock artwork. When the real backend is wired, navigating to `/media` will silently show mock art instead of the real image/video. Also: any `kind` value outside `image/video/document` (e.g. `audio`) silently falls through to the document viewer.
---
**7. `ChatRichScreen` shows wrong mock data for real conversation IDs — `chat_rich_screen.dart` line ~83**
Any `conversationId` that isn't literally `'rose'`, `'mike'`, or `'fam'` silently displays "Family Member" and a generic message thread with no loading/error state. When real backend UUIDs are passed, users see stale mock data with no indication anything is wrong.
---
**8. `.env` not excluded from `remote_deploy.py` upload — `deploy/remote_deploy.py`**
`SKIP_FILES` excludes `firebase-service-account.json` and `google-services.json` but not `.env`. The intent is to upload `.env` to the server (correct), but there's no guardrail preventing `git add .env`. Add `.env` to the repo's root `.gitignore` (it's already in `.gitignore` for the backend dir) and add an assertion in the deploy script that `.env` is not git-tracked before uploading.
---
### ⚪ Low / Maintenance
**9. Dead code in `auth_notifier._tryRestoreSession` — `auth_notifier.dart` line 34**
The `if (AppConfig.uiOnly) { … return; }` guard inside `_tryRestoreSession` is unreachable — the constructor's `else` branch already prevents calling the method when `uiOnly` is true. Safe to delete; it's a maintenance trap if the constructor is ever refactored.
---
**10. `file_picker` pinned to exact version — `pubspec.yaml` line 42**
`file_picker: 11.0.2` (no `^`) deviates from every other dependency. If this version is retracted from pub.dev or conflicts with a transitive constraint, `pub get` fails with no fallback. Change to `file_picker: ^11.0.2`.
---
## Overall Assessment
| Area | Status |
|---|---|
| Backend API logic | ✅ Solid — routers, auth, messaging all correct except the calls prefix bug |
| Backend security | ⚠️ Two unauthenticated info-disclosure issues on `/health`, exception message leak |
| Deploy scripts | 🔴 TURN secret committed in plaintext — rotate immediately |
| Flutter architecture | ✅ GoRouter refresh pattern, Riverpod providers, theme migration all correct |
| Flutter UI | ✅ Design system fully migrated to `core/theme/`, nginx cleaned up, no stale imports |
| Flutter–backend wiring | ⚠️ `uiOnly=true` default + call/chat screens are mock-only stubs — intentional for now but dangerous default |
| New features (calls/chats) | ✅ Well-structured visual shells, no compile errors, WebRTC correctly deferred |
The backend is live and the code quality is good. The two things that need immediate action before real users: **rotate the TURN secret** and **flip the `uiOnly` default to `false`**.

## Goal

survive offline (queued locally, synced on reconnect), show single/double ticks,
typing, and online/last-seen status, and support photos, videos, documents, and voice
notes.

## Tasks

### 1. `core/services/signaling_service.dart`

The Socket.IO client wrapper (shared with calling in prompt 14):
- Connect to `AppConfig.signalingUrl` with `path: '/signal'`, `transports:['websocket']`,
  auth `{ token: <accessToken> }`.
- Reconnection config: `enableReconnection`, infinite attempts, delay 1s → max 10s,
  randomization factor 0.5, timeout 20s.
- Expose typed streams/callbacks for: `message:new`, `message:deleted`, `message:ack`,

  (`call:incoming` etc.) which prompt 14 consumes.
- Emit helpers: `emitTyping(start/stop, to)`, `emitPresence(status)`,
  `requestPresence(userIds)`.
- Reconnect handling: on `connect`/`reconnect`, fire a callback the `SyncService` uses;
  on `disconnect`, mark presence stale.
- Re-attach the (possibly refreshed) access token on reconnect.

### 2. `core/services/sync_service.dart`

  the REST API in order, mark synced on success.

  newest locally-stored message (cursor/`since`), upsert into Drift.
- `syncConversations()` — refresh the conversation list from `GET /api/conversations`.
- Trigger all three on socket reconnect and on app resume.

### 3. `features/chat/` structure

```

  data/
    message_repository.dart
    message_local_dao.dart      # thin wrapper over Drift MessagesDao
  domain/

    media_viewer_screen.dart

      message_bubble.dart
      media_message.dart
      voice_note_player.dart
      voice_note_recorder.dart
      typing_indicator.dart
      chat_input_bar.dart
```

### 4. `message_repository.dart`

- `sendMessage(...)` → `POST /api/messages` (always include the client-generated
  `client_id` UUID).
- `fetchMessages(conversationId, cursor)` → `GET /api/conversations/{id}/messages`.
- `listConversations()` → `GET /api/conversations`.

  opens `/contacts` to start a new chat.

skills.name: code-review
skills.content:
Review target: `--effort max`

`high effort → 3 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 angles, up to 6 each)

Run **3 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`.

Complete implementation of the Flutter messaging feature:

Core services
- SignalingService: Socket.IO client with typed event streams (MessageNewEvent,
  MessageAckEvent, PresenceEvent, TypingEvent, CallIncomingEvent); auto-connects
  on auth token change; exposes onReconnect hook for SyncService
- SyncService: syncPendingMessages (oldest-first outbox flush), fetchMissedMessages
  (cursor-based catch-up), syncConversations (conversation + profile cache refresh)
- NotificationService: showMessageNotification for foreground FCM messages

Data layer
- MessageLocalDao: domain↔Drift conversion, watchMessages/upsertMessage/markSynced/
  updateStatus/markDeleted/clearUnread/getPendingUploads
- MessageRepository: sendMessage, fetchMessages (cursor pagination), markDelivered,
  markRead, deleteMessage, uploadMedia (multipart with progress callback)
- AppDatabase: added forTesting(QueryExecutor) constructor for unit tests

Domain
- ChatNotifier (FamilyNotifier<ChatState, conversationId>): optimistic write to
  Drift before network; failed sends marked for retry; socket subscriptions for
  new/ack/deleted/typing events; paginated history load; debounced typing emit
- ConversationListNotifier: Drift-backed list, live presence updates, socket
  refresh on message:new
- PresenceProvider: seeds from Drift, requests via socket, streams live updates

Presentation
- ChatScreen: full-featured chat UI with date separators, loading indicator,
  typing indicator, reply bar, video/voice call action buttons
- ConversationListScreen: AsyncValue-driven list with unread badge, online dot,
  pull-to-refresh, empty state
- MediaViewerScreen: photo_view pinch-zoom for images; video_player for video;
  transparent app bar with metadata
- Widgets: MessageBubble (status ticks, long-press menu, deleted tombstone),
  ChatInputBar (media picker, voice recorder toggle), TypingIndicator (3-dot
  bounce), VoiceNotePlayer, VoiceNoteRecorder (hold-to-record, slide-to-cancel),
  MediaMessage (image/video/audio/file dispatch)

App wiring
- app.dart: new ChatScreen/MediaViewerScreen routes; LuminApp WidgetsBindingObserver
  for app-resume sync; FCM cold-start deep-link consumption on first frame
- main.dart: FCM getInitialMessage + onMessageOpenedApp deep-link handlers;
  foreground FCM → showMessageNotification; pendingDeepLinkProvider
- shell_screen.dart: Messages tab now uses ConversationListScreen (replaces mock)

Tests
- chat_notifier_test.dart: optimistic send, network failure, socket dedup, ack ticks
- sync_service_test.dart: oldest-first ordering, success→isSynced, error tolerance,
  empty outbox guard

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

content.text:
Prompt 13 is fully implemented and committed (`530b6bc`). Here's the complete picture of what was delivered:

---

## Prompt 13 — Complete ✅

### What was done

**Shell update**
- `shell_screen.dart` — Messages tab now renders `ConversationListScreen` (replaces the old mock `ChatsHomeScreen`)

**Core services**
- `SignalingService` — Socket.IO wrapper with typed event streams; auto-connects/disconnects on auth token change
- `SyncService` — outbox flush (oldest-first), missed-message catch-up, conversation cache refresh
- `NotificationService` — `showMessageNotification` for foreground FCM messages

**Data layer**
- `MessageLocalDao` — Drift ↔ domain `Message` conversion; all read/write operations
- `MessageRepository` — send, fetch (cursor paginated), receipts, delete, media upload
- `AppDatabase` — added `forTesting(QueryExecutor)` constructor

**Domain**
- `ChatNotifier` (`FamilyNotifier`) — optimistic Drift write before HTTP; socket subscriptions for new/ack/deleted/typing; paginated history; debounced typing emit; retry on failure
- `ConversationListNotifier` — Drift-backed list with live presence and socket refresh
- `PresenceProvider` — Drift seed → socket request → live stream

**Presentation (17 files)**
- `ChatScreen`, `ConversationListScreen`, `MediaViewerScreen`
- Widgets: `MessageBubble` (status ticks ⏱→✓→✓✓→✓✓🔵→⚠), `ChatInputBar`, `TypingIndicator`, `VoiceNotePlayer`, `VoiceNoteRecorder`, `MediaMessage`

**Tests**
- `chat_notifier_test.dart` — 4 tests: optimistic send, network failure, socket dedup, receipt tick
- `sync_service_test.dart` — 4 tests: oldest-first ordering, success→`isSynced`, error tolerance, empty-outbox guard

### One thing still pending on the server
The leaked TURN secret (`80c0816f…`) should be rotated:
```bash
# On the VPS:
export NEW_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
# update TURN_SECRET= in /opt/lumin/.env
# then: bash coturn/install.sh
```

Push to remote whenever you're ready — just run `git push origin main` in the repo directory.

Here's what happened and why it's fully resolved now:

---

## What the problem actually was

The real villain wasn't Riverpod — it was the **outdated Flutter SDK (3.38.9)**. That version shipped a `flutter_test` that hard-pins `test_api` to exactly `0.7.7`. Riverpod 3.x transitively pulls in `test ^1.0.0`, which needs `test_api ≥ 0.7.8`. With the old SDK those two were irreconcilable regardless of what else you changed.

## What was fixed

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| `flutter upgrade` → **3.44.0 / Dart 3.12.0** | `test_api` pin lifted from `0.7.7` → `0.7.11`; conflict dissolved |
| `pub upgrade --major-versions` | Drift 2.33, SQLite 3.3.1, analyzer 12.1, win32 6.3, file_picker 12 |
| `pub upgrade` | `synchronized` micro-bump picked up |

## Current state

- ✅ All **direct and dev dependencies** are at their latest resolvable versions  
- ✅ `riverpod ^3.3.1` resolves cleanly with no workarounds  
- ✅ The `riverpod_annotation`/`riverpod_generator` removal stays — those packages were genuinely unused  
- ℹ️ 19 **transitive** packages show newer versions in `pub outdated` — these are all constrained by *their* parents (e.g. `flutter_sound_platform_interface 10.x` needs `flutter_sound 10.x` which we don't use yet). That's normal and not actionable.

**Going forward:** run `flutter upgrade` periodically to keep the SDK current — that's the single biggest lever for keeping the whole ecosystem compatible.

skills.name: code-review
skills.content:
Review target: `--effort max`

`high effort → 3 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 angles, up to 6 each)

Run **3 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`.

684	class _SwipeToReplyWrapperState extends State<_SwipeToReplyWrapper> with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
685	  late final AnimationController _ctrl;
686	  double _dragOffset = 0;
687	
688	  @override
689	  void initState() {
690	    super.initState();
691	    _ctrl = AnimationController(vsync: this, duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 200));
692	    _ctrl.addListener(() {
693	      setState(() {
694	        _dragOffset = _dragOffset * (1 - _ctrl.value);
695	      });
696	    });
697	  }

699	  @override
700	  void dispose() {
701	    _ctrl.dispose();
702	    super.dispose();
703	  }

705	  @override
706	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
707	    return GestureDetector(
708	      onHorizontalDragUpdate: (details) {
709	        if (details.primaryDelta! > 0 || _dragOffset > 0) {
710	          setState(() {
711	            _dragOffset += details.primaryDelta!;
712	            if (_dragOffset < 0) _dragOffset = 0;
713	            if (_dragOffset > 60) _dragOffset = 60 + (_dragOffset - 60) * 0.2;
714	          });
715	        }
716	      },
717	      onHorizontalDragEnd: (details) {
718	        if (_dragOffset > 40) {
719	          widget.onSwipe();
720	        }
721	        _ctrl.forward(from: 0);
722	      },
723	      child: Transform.translate(
724	        offset: Offset(_dragOffset, 0),
725	        child: widget.child,
726	      ),
727	    );
728	  }

1304	// Matches exactly the CSS border-radius values in the HTML spec:
1305	//   sent:     20px 20px 6px 20px  (TL TR BR BL) → bottom-right is tail

1308	BorderRadius _bubbleRadius(bool mine) => mine
1309	    ? const BorderRadius.only(
1310	        topLeft:     Radius.circular(_T.bigR),

1312	        bottomLeft:  Radius.circular(_T.bigR),
1313	        bottomRight: Radius.circular(_T.tailR),
1314	      )
1315	    : const BorderRadius.only(
1316	        topLeft:     Radius.circular(_T.bigR),

1322	// ─── Dashed border painter ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1323	// Flutter has no built-in dashed-border support; this CustomPainter draws
1324	// the rounded-rectangle dashed outline used by the deleted-message bubble.
1325	
1326	class _DashedBorderPainter extends CustomPainter {
1327	  const _DashedBorderPainter({
1328	    required this.color,
1329	    required this.radius,
1330	    required this.dashLength,
1331	    required this.gapLength,
1332	    required this.strokeWidth,
1333	  });
1334	
1335	  final Color  color;
1336	  final double radius;
1337	  final double dashLength;
1338	  final double gapLength;
1339	  final double strokeWidth;
1340	
1341	  @override
1342	  void paint(Canvas canvas, Size size) {
1343	    final paint = Paint()
1344	      ..color       = color
1345	      ..strokeWidth = strokeWidth
1346	      ..style       = PaintingStyle.stroke;
1347	
1348	    final rrect = RRect.fromRectAndRadius(
1349	      Rect.fromLTWH(strokeWidth / 2, strokeWidth / 2,
1350	          size.width - strokeWidth, size.height - strokeWidth),
1351	      Radius.circular(radius),
1352	    );
1353	
1354	    final path         = Path()..addRRect(rrect);
1355	    final metrics      = path.computeMetrics().first;
1356	    final totalLength  = metrics.length;
1357	
1358	    double dist = 0;
1359	    bool   draw = true;
1360	
1361	    while (dist < totalLength) {
1362	      final segLen = draw ? dashLength : gapLength;
1363	      if (draw) {
1364	        canvas.drawPath(
1365	          metrics.extractPath(dist, math.min(dist + segLen, totalLength)),
1366	          paint,
1367	        );
1368	      }
1369	      dist += segLen;
1370	      draw  = !draw;
1371	    }
1372	  }
1373	
1374	  @override
1375	  bool shouldRepaint(_DashedBorderPainter old) =>
1376	      old.color       != color       ||
1377	      old.radius      != radius      ||
1378	      old.dashLength  != dashLength  ||
1379	      old.gapLength   != gapLength   ||
1380	      old.strokeWidth != strokeWidth;
1381	}
